title: Missed Opportunities for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Prescription in French Military Primary Care: A KAP Survey With Scenario-Based Modeling
abstract: Abstract Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, yet uptake remains suboptimal. In France, routine vaccination targets early adolescence (11-14 years), with catch-up vaccination recommended up to age 26 years. Reimbursement extension to age 26 became effective in December 2025, after the present survey. Within the French Military Health Service (Service de Santé des Armées, SSA), HPV vaccines are generally not administered in primary care units; prevention therefore relies on identifying eligible service members and initiating vaccination through prescription and referral to community-based administration. Materials and Methods A cross-sectional, anonymous online Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) survey was conducted in September 2025 among active-duty SSA military general practitioners (MGPs). The primary outcome was self-reported routine initiation of HPV vaccination via prescription. Responses were dichotomized as “Yes” versus “No.” Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to identify individual factors associated with HPV vaccine prescription. Barriers (non-prescribers) and implementation difficulties (prescribers) were described. Model-based scenario analyses estimated predicted probabilities of routine initiation under modifiable levers (increased opportunities via prompts/standardized visits, comfort with sexual-health discussions, and HPV knowledge), with uncertainty assessed using non-parametric bootstrap (500 resamples). Results Among approximately 800 active-duty military physicians contacted through institutional channels, 186 completed the survey and met the inclusion criteria for the present analysis, corresponding to approximately one quarter of contacted physicians. Among respondents, 70 (38%) reported routinely initiating HPV vaccination. Routine initiation was independently associated with gynecology-related clinical activity within the unit (aOR 2.53, 95% CI 1.03-6.46) and higher HPV knowledge (aOR 1.17 per point, 95% CI 1.02-1.36), and inversely associated with difficulty discussing sexual health (aOR 0.30, 95% CI 0.13-0.64). Sociodemographic characteristics were similar between groups. Among non-prescribers, the leading barrier was omission (“I don’t think about it,” 65%), followed by lack of an on-site delivery pathway (“vaccine unavailability within the unit,” 47%); fear of refusal was uncommon. Scenario analyses suggested larger gains from increasing opportunities (routinized prompts/standardized encounters) and improving communication comfort than from knowledge gains alone, with additive effects when combining levers. Conclusions In SSA primary care, routine initiation of HPV vaccination via prescription appears constrained mainly by missed opportunities and organizational friction rather than clinician opposition. With expanded catch-up recommendations and extended reimbursement up to age 26 years, implementation efforts within the French armed forces are timely; systematic prompts, streamlined prescription-to-vaccination pathways, and brief communication-focused training may increase initiation rates.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of French military general practitioners (MGPs) regarding human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. The research aimed to understand the barriers to HPV vaccine prescription within the French Military Health Service (SSA). A cross-sectional, anonymous online KAP survey was conducted in September 2025 among approximately 800 MGPs, with 186 completing the survey. The primary outcome was self-reported routine initiation of HPV vaccination via prescription, with 70 (38%) reporting this practice. The study found that routine initiation was associated with gynecology-related clinical activity, higher HPV knowledge, and comfort in discussing sexual health. Scenario-based modeling suggested that increasing opportunities for vaccination and improving communication comfort could lead to greater initiation rates. The findings highlight the importance of addressing organizational and systemic barriers to HPV vaccination in military primary care settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 可预防 HPV 相关癌症,但摄取量仍不理想。在法国,常规 疫苗接种 针对青春期早期(11-14 岁),建议追赶 疫苗接种 直至 26 岁。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2025 年 9 月,对现役法国军事卫生局 (SSA) 军事全科医生 (MGP) 进行了一项横断面匿名在线知识、态度和实践 (KAP) 调查。回答分为“是”和“否”。进行单变量和多变量分析以确定与 HPV 疫苗 处方相关的个体因素。
elements_zh.methods: 主要结果是自我报告的通过处方常规启动 HPV 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.main_results: 在通过机构渠道联系的约 800 名现役军医中,有 186 名完成了调查并符合本分析的纳入标准,相当于约四分之一的联系医生。在受访者中,70 人 (38%) 报告定期启动 HPV 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过处方常规启动 HPV 疫苗接种 似乎主要受到错失机会和组织摩擦的限制,而不是临床医生的反对。情景分析表明,与单独获得知识相比,增加机会(常规提示/标准化遭遇)和提高沟通舒适度可以获得更大的收益,并且在组合杠杆时会产生附加效应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 随着追赶建议的扩大和报销期限延长至 26 岁,法国武装部队内部的实施工作非常及时。系统的提示、简化的从处方到 疫苗接种 的路径以及简短的以沟通为重点的培训可能会提高启动率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告与研究设计或证据强度相关的具体限制。

title: Diagnostic utility of high‐risk HPV polymerase chain reaction–based testing in head and neck FNA specimens with indeterminate cytomorphology
abstract: Abstract Background Fine‐needle aspiration (FNA) is critical in the initial diagnosis of many high‐risk human papillomavirus (HR‐HPV)–associated, metastatic oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinomas. Updated guidelines recommend HR‐HPV–specific polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis over p16 immunohistochemistry on FNA specimens because p16 performs poorly on cytology material. PCR‐based assays on liquid cytology material have demonstrated excellent analytic performance; however, the diagnostic utility of a positive HR‐HPV PCR result in specimens with indeterminate cytomorphology remains uncharacterized. Methods The authors retrospectively identified 279 head and neck FNA specimens that had paired HR‐HPV PCR testing on residual liquid cytology material over a 5‐year period. The positive predictive value for histopathologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma on surgical follow‐up was calculated within each cytologic interpretive category. Results The HR‐HPV PCR results were positive in 50.2% of specimens, negative in 40.9%, and indeterminate in 9.0%. The HR‐HPV positivity rate ranged from 0% in specimens categorized as negative for malignancy to 57.3% in cytologically positive specimens, with 19.0%, 41.2%, and 50.0% positivity in the atypical, suspicious, and nondiagnostic categories, respectively. Among cytologically indeterminate specimens with positive HR‐HPV PCR results ( n = 14), the positive predictive value was 100% (95% confidence interval, 78.5%–100.0%). Blinded slide review additionally identified 15 cytologically positive specimens in which the definitive malignant interpretation depended substantially on HR‐HPV positivity; all 15 were confirmed as squamous cell carcinoma. Conclusions A positive HR‐HPV PCR result on liquid cytology material carries a positive predictive value of 100% for malignancy in cytologically indeterminate head and neck FNA specimens. These findings support integrating HR‐HPV PCR analysis into routine cytologic interpretation with the potential to upgrade some indeterminate specimens to malignant when HR‐HPV is detected, expediting definitive treatment and sparing patients additional, invasive sampling.

title: Real-World Effectiveness and Impact of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination in Males: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gender-neutral vaccination (GNV) for human papillomavirus (HPV) has increasingly been implemented worldwide. However, real-world evidence on vaccine effectiveness (VE) in males and the population-level impact of GNV remains heterogeneous. We summarized real-world VE of HPV vaccination in males and the impact of GNV. METHODS: A comprehensive review was performed using Embase and PubMed from January 2007 to May 2024, for studies evaluating quadrivalent (4vHPV) or nonavalent (9vHPV) vaccines. Eligible studies assessed VE or GNV impact on HPV infections, precancerous lesions, cancer, or anogenital warts (AGW). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and the National Institute of Health quality assessment tool. RESULTS: Twenty-one geographically diverse studies were included. Most VE and VI studies demonstrated risk of bias. In males, VE reached up to 100% against oral HPV infection and 41% for penile HPV (4vHPV genotypes), with higher VE among adolescents and those vaccinated before age 23. Among men who have sex with men, VE was higher for penile HPV infection (85%), AGW (55%), and anal infection (60%). CONCLUSIONS: Real-world evidence indicates that HPV vaccination substantially reduces anogenital and oral HPV infections and AGW in males. GNV programs further reduce HPV-related disease burden, reinforcing the public health significance of universal HPV vaccination programs worldwide.

title: Clearance of high‐risk human papillomavirus in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2–3 after the loop electrosurgical excision procedure with negative resection margins
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aims to evaluate the longitudinal clearance rates of high‐risk human papillomavirus (hr‐HPV) and the incidence of clinical recurrence (defined by abnormal cytology or histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia; CIN) at 6 and 18 months post‐loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP), characterizing the mathematical boundaries within the complete cohort. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University. We evaluated the clinical records of 145 patients diagnosed with CIN 2–3 who underwent LEEP between January 2021 and December 2024, analyzing clearance and clinical outcomes over an 18‐month surveillance window. Results The baseline prevalence of hr‐HPV was 99.3% ( n = 144/145). At 6 months post‐LEEP, the type‐specific viral clearance rate was 74.3% ( n = 107/144). At 18 months, complete hr‐HPV negativity was 75.8% (47/62) among the evaluable subcohort, representing a conservative baseline minimum of 32.6% (47/144) when accounting for complete attrition bounds. The overall recurrence rate of CIN or cytological abnormalities was 11.1% (16/144). Notably, 15 of 16 recurrences were detected at the 6‐month interval, of which 73.3% (11/15) demonstrated concurrent hr‐HPV positivity ( P = 0.0001). Conclusion Loop electrosurgical excision procedure facilitates significant viral clearance, but persistent hr‐HPV serves as a potent biomarker for clinical recurrence. Implementing mandatory HPV‐based testing at the 6‐month follow‐up window optimizes risk stratification, providing critical data to guide surveillance in the presence of follow‐up limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估宫颈上皮内瘤变 2-3 患者在环路电切手术 (LEEP) 后高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (hr-HPV) 的纵向清除率和临床复发的 发病率,从而解决了解 治疗 后结果的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 玛希隆大学 Siriraj 医院进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,涉及 145 名诊断为 CIN 2-3 的患者,这些患者在 2021 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月期间接受了 LEEP,监测 窗口期为 18 个月。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究分析了诊断为 CIN 2-3 并接受 LEEP 的患者的临床记录,重点关注 hr-HPV 清除率和由异常细胞学或组织学证实的 CIN 定义的临床复发。
elements_zh.main_results: hr-HPV 的基线 患病率 为 99.3% (n = 144/145)。LEEP 后 6 个月,类型特异性病毒清除率为 74.3% (n = 107/144)。18 个月时,可评估亚组中 hr-HPV 完全阴性率为 75.8% (47/62),考虑到完全流失界限时,保守基线最小值为 32.6% (47/144)。CIN 或细胞学异常的总体复发率为 11.1% (16/144),其中 16 例复发中有 15 例在 6 个月的间隔内检测到,其中 73.3% (11/15) 表现出并发 hr-HPV 阳性 (P = 0.0001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,LEEP 有助于显着的病毒清除,但持续存在的 hr-HPV 可作为临床复发的有效生物标志物,强调了其在风险分层中的潜在作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在 6 个月的随访窗口中进行基于 HPV 的检测对于优化风险分层并在随访限制的情况下指导 监测 策略的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的自然减员而受到限制,保守估计 18 个月时 hr-HPV 清除率为 32.6%。由于这些限制,证据是中等的。

title: Factors impacting protective immunity conferred by vaccination with adeno-associated virus-like particles displaying human papillomavirus L2 residues 17–36
abstract: ABSTRACT A phase I study was conducted in 20 healthy subjects with 20 μg adeno-associated virus 2 (AAV2)-like particles displaying L2 residues 17–36 of both human papillomavirus (HPV) type 16 and HPV31 (AAVLP-HPV) or placebo. AAVLP-HPV vaccination was well tolerated and induced a modest L2-specific serum antibody titer that neutralizes HPV16, HPV31, and HPV5 in vitro . Here, we show that upon passive transfer into naïve mice, the sera from a subset of patients vaccinated with AAVLP-HPV conferred protection against HPV16, HPV31, and HPV5, but not HPV76. HPV16-naïve patients required three AAVLP-HPV doses to develop protection, whereas previously exposed individuals achieved protection after two doses and exhibited higher L2-specific and neutralizing antibody titers. The avidity of the L2-specific antibody response was low, but broadly cross-reactive. Prior exposure to AAV2 compromised the strength and duration of the L2 neutralizing antibody response, as well as protective immunity against HPV16, suggesting original antigenic sin. AAVLP-HPV induced high AAV2 neutralizing titers after one vaccination in AAV2-exposed or three in AAV2-naive patients. Thus, prior HPV and AAV2 infections impact the interpretation of AAVLP-HPV immunogenicity. IMPORTANCE HPV is among the most prevalent sexually transmitted infections. Persistent infection with a high-risk genotype (hrHPV) can cause cervical and other anogenital, and oropharyngeal cancers. There are a dozen hrHPV genotypes, HPV16 being the dominant type in these cancers; only ≤7 are targeted by licensed HPV vaccines. Ten intermediate-risk genotypes are also found in small proportions of cervical cancers. HPV6 and HPV11, while commonly associated with benign genital warts, can be carcinogenic in humans. The HPV+ cancer burden is highest in developing countries where cervical screening and vaccination rates are low, resulting in >500,000 cervical cancer cases annually. The plethora of skin-tropic HPVs are transmitted non-sexually and generally cause benign, self-limiting infections, but a subset of betapapillomavirus es is associated with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma in epidermodysplasia verruciformis and immunocompromised patients. A simple, low-cost vaccine preventing infection by all of these medically significant HPV types is needed. CLINICAL TRIALS This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT03929172 .

title_original: Factors impacting protective immunity conferred by vaccination with adeno-associated virus-like particles displaying human papillomavirus L2 residues 17–36

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of vaccination with adeno-associated virus-like particles (AAVLP-HPV) displaying HPV L2 residues 17–36 on protective immunity against HPV16, HPV31, and HPV5. The background highlights the prevalence of HPV infections and the limited coverage of current vaccines against certain high-risk and intermediate-risk genotypes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A phase I study was conducted in 20 healthy subjects, with 20 μg of AAVLP-HPV or placebo administered. The study involved both HPV-naïve and previously exposed individuals to assess differences in immune response and protective immunity.
analysis.methods: The study used passive transfer of sera from vaccinated individuals into naïve mice to evaluate protection against HPV16, HPV31, and HPV5. It also compared the antibody titers and neutralizing responses between HPV-naïve and previously exposed participants.
analysis.main_results: Sera from a subset of patients vaccinated with AAVLP-HPV conferred protection against HPV16, HPV31, and HPV5, but not HPV76. HPV16-naïve patients required three doses to develop protection, while previously exposed individuals achieved it after two doses and had higher L2-specific and neutralizing antibody titers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that prior exposure to HPV and AAV2 may influence the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of AAVLP-HPV, potentially due to original antigenic sin. This study provides novel insights into how immune history affects vaccine response.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results have implications for understanding vaccine efficacy in populations with varying HPV exposure histories, which could inform strategies for improving immunization programs and addressing disparities in protection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and reliance on passive transfer in mice, which may not fully reflect human immune responses. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on in vitro neutralization and animal models.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the protective immunity induced by vaccination with adeno-associated virus-like particles (AAVLP-HPV) displaying HPV L2 residues 17–36 against HPV16, HPV31, and HPV5. A phase I trial in 20 healthy subjects showed that AAVLP-HPV was well tolerated and induced modest antibody titers. Passive transfer experiments in mice revealed that sera from vaccinated individuals could confer protection against certain HPV types but not HPV76. HPV16-naïve participants required three doses for protection, while previously exposed individuals needed only two. The study highlights the impact of prior HPV and AAV2 infections on vaccine-induced immunity, suggesting original antigenic sin. These findings are relevant for improving vaccine strategies and understanding immune responses in diverse populations. However, the study's small sample size and use of animal models limit the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估 疫苗接种 与显示 HPV L2 残基 17-36 的腺相关病毒样颗粒 (AAVLP-HPV) 对 HPV16、HPV31 和 HPV5 的保护性免疫的影响。背景突出了 HPV 感染的 患病率 以及当前 疫苗 针对某些高风险和中风险基因型的有限覆盖范围。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: I 期研究在 20 名健康受试者中进行,给予 20 μg AAVLP-HPV 或安慰剂。该研究涉及未接触过 HPV 的个体和之前接触过 HPV 的个体,以评估 免疫应答 和保护性免疫的差异。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究将接种疫苗的个体的血清被动转移到幼鼠体内,以评估对 HPV16、HPV31 和 HPV5 的保护作用。它还比较了未接触过 HPV 的参与者和之前接触过 HPV 的参与者之间的抗体滴度和中和反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 来自接种 AAVLP-HPV 疫苗的一部分患者的血清可提供针对 HPV16、HPV31 和 HPV5 的保护,但不提供针对 HPV76 的保护。未感染 HPV16 的患者需要注射 3 剂才能产生保护作用,而之前接触过 HPV16 的患者在注射 2 剂后即可达到保护效果,并且具有更高的 L2 特异性和中和抗体滴度。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,先前接触 HPV 和 AAV2 可能会影响 AAVLP-HPV 的免疫原性和保护功效,这可能是由于原始抗原原罪所致。这项研究提供了关于免疫史如何影响 疫苗 反应的新见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解 疫苗 在具有不同 HPV 暴露史的人群中的功效具有重要意义,这可以为改进免疫计划和解决保护差异的策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小和依赖小鼠被动转移的限制,可能无法完全反映人类的 免疫应答。证据是中等的,因为这些发现是基于体外中和和动物模型。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估 疫苗接种 与显示 HPV L2 残基 17-36 的腺相关病毒样颗粒 (AAVLP-HPV) 对 HPV16、HPV31 和 HPV5 的保护性免疫的影响。背景突出了 HPV 感染的 患病率 以及当前 疫苗 针对某些高风险和中风险基因型的有限覆盖范围。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: I 期研究在 20 名健康受试者中进行,给予 20 μg AAVLP-HPV 或安慰剂。该研究涉及未接触过 HPV 的个体和之前接触过 HPV 的个体,以评估 免疫应答 和保护性免疫的差异。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究将接种疫苗的个体的血清被动转移到幼鼠体内,以评估对 HPV16、HPV31 和 HPV5 的保护作用。它还比较了未接触过 HPV 的参与者和之前接触过 HPV 的参与者之间的抗体滴度和中和反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 来自接种 AAVLP-HPV 疫苗的一部分患者的血清可提供针对 HPV16、HPV31 和 HPV5 的保护,但不提供针对 HPV76 的保护。未感染 HPV16 的患者需要注射 3 剂才能产生保护作用,而之前接触过 HPV16 的患者在注射 2 剂后即可达到保护效果,并且具有更高的 L2 特异性和中和抗体滴度。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,先前接触 HPV 和 AAV2 可能会影响 AAVLP-HPV 的免疫原性和保护功效,这可能是由于原始抗原原罪所致。这项研究提供了关于免疫史如何影响 疫苗 反应的新见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果对于了解 疫苗 在具有不同 HPV 暴露史的人群中的功效具有重要意义,这可以为改进免疫计划和解决保护差异的策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小和依赖小鼠被动转移的限制,可能无法完全反映人类的 免疫应答。证据是中等的,因为这些发现是基于体外中和和动物模型。

title: Incidence and Prevalence of Human Papillomavirus Infection to Predict Outcomes from HPV-Based Cervical Cancer Screening in Women and People with a Cervix Living with HIV
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing has been implemented in many organized cervix screening programs; however, understanding how this screening methodology affects rates of colposcopy and further follow-up procedures remains underexplored, especially among women with HIV. In the absence of HPV screening program data in British Columbia (BC), Canada, we sought to determine HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopies among a cohort of women with HIV using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm. Setting: HPV data were collected and analyzed from a prospective HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort study of women with HIV from 14 sites of HIV care across Canada from 2008 to 2015. Methods: HPV data were obtained during the screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 time points (Linear Array assay). Participant demographic and clinical characteristics (CD4 + count, HIV viral load, etc.) were assessed to determine associations between HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopy using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening which would result in a colposcopy referral. In total, 15.9% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24 time points, which would result in 3 consecutive referrals to colposcopy. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detected were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load compared with participants without oncogenic HPV detected. Conclusions: Results of this study suggest that HPV testing will result in a high proportion of referrals to colposcopy and follow-up procedures among women with HIV, which will require preparation and planning. Further work is needed to provide the appropriate support and education for women with HIV when incorporating HPV testing into cervix screening programs.
journal: JAIDS Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer screening programs increasingly use HPV testing, but its downstream impact on colposcopy referrals in women with HIV remains poorly understood, creating uncertainty for program planning and resource allocation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective cohort study analyzed HPV data from a Canadian immunogenicity cohort of women with HIV across 14 HIV care sites from 2008 to 2015 to estimate HPV prevalence and colposcopy referral rates using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm.
analysis.methods: HPV status was determined at screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 using the Linear Array assay, and associations with colposcopy referral were assessed using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals alongside participant demographic and clinical characteristics.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, which would result in a colposcopy referral, and 15.9% had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24, indicating three consecutive referrals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as indicating that HPV testing will lead to a high burden of colposcopy referrals among women with HIV, necessitating preparation and planning for program implementation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results suggest that HPV-based screening in women with HIV may substantially increase colposcopy demand, requiring targeted support and education to optimize program delivery and patient outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single Canadian cohort and the absence of program-level data, which constrains generalizability and underscores the need for broader implementation studies to confirm these findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of HPV testing on colposcopy referral rates among women with HIV in Canada using a prospective cohort design spanning 2008–2015. It found that 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV at screening, warranting colposcopy referral, and 15.9% had persistent oncogenic HPV across three time points, indicating repeated referrals. The authors conclude that HPV-based screening will likely increase colposcopy demand in this population, necessitating programmatic preparation. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the single-cohort design and lack of broader implementation data.

title_zh: 发病率 和 患病率 的 人乳头瘤病毒 感染可预测女性和宫颈 HIV 感染者基于 HPV 的 宫颈癌 筛查结果
source_body_en: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing has been implemented in many organized cervix screening programs; however, understanding how this screening methodology affects rates of colposcopy and further follow-up procedures remains underexplored, especially among women with HIV. In the absence of HPV screening program data in British Columbia (BC), Canada, we sought to determine HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopies among a cohort of women with HIV using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm. Setting: HPV data were collected and analyzed from a prospective HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort study of women with HIV from 14 sites of HIV care across Canada from 2008 to 2015. Methods: HPV data were obtained during the screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 time points (Linear Array assay). Participant demographic and clinical characteristics (CD4 + count, HIV viral load, etc.) were assessed to determine associations between HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopy using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening which would result in a colposcopy referral. In total, 15.9% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24 time points, which would result in 3 consecutive referrals to colposcopy. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detected were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load compared with participants without oncogenic HPV detected. Conclusions: Results of this study suggest that HPV testing will result in a high proportion of referrals to colposcopy and follow-up procedures among women with HIV, which will require preparation and planning. Further work is needed to provide the appropriate support and education for women with HIV when incorporating HPV testing into cervix screening programs.
abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 检测已在许多有组织的子宫颈筛查计划中实施;然而,了解这种筛查方法如何影响阴道镜检查率和进一步的随访程序仍有待探索,特别是在感染艾滋病毒的女性中。由于加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省 (BC) 缺乏 HPV 筛查计划数据,我们试图使用 BC 子宫颈筛查算法确定感染 HIV 的 队列研究 女性中的 HPV 患病率 和阴道镜检查的估计值。背景:HPV 数据是从 2008 年至 2015 年加拿大 14 个 HIV 护理地点的 HIV 感染女性的前瞻性 HPV 疫苗 免疫原性 队列研究 研究中收集和分析的。方法:在筛查(第 -3 个月)、基线(第 0 个月)、第 12 个月和第 24 个月时间点(线性阵列测定)期间获得 HPV 数据。评估参与者的人口统计和临床特征(CD4 + 计数、HIV 病毒载量等),以确定 HPV 患病率 与使用比率和 95% 置信区间的阴道镜检查估计值之间的关联。结果:总体而言,47.2% 的参与者在筛查时检测到致癌 HPV,这将导致转诊阴道镜检查。总共有 15.9% 的参与者在筛查、第 12 个月和第 24 个月的时间点检测到致癌 HPV,这将导致连续 3 次转诊进行阴道镜检查。与未检测到致癌 HPV 的参与者相比,重复检测到致癌 HPV 的参与者 HIV 病毒载量受到抑制的可能性较小。结论:这项研究的结果表明,HPV 检测将导致 HIV 感染女性中较高比例的转诊到阴道镜检查和后续程序,这需要做好准备和规划。将 HPV 检测纳入子宫颈筛查计划时,需要开展进一步的工作,为感染艾滋病毒的女性提供适当的支持和教育。

title: Human papillomavirus 42: from a low-risk genotype to a potentially oncogenic virus.
abstract: Human papillomavirus 42 (HPV42), initially classified as a low-risk genotype isolated from benign vulvar papillomas, has long been associated with benign lesions such as anogenital warts. However, recent studies have uncovered its unexpected oncogenic potential, challenging its traditional classification. HPV42 has been identified as a causative driver of digital papillary adenocarcinoma, a rare and aggressive cutaneous tumour, and is also linked to high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions in the cervix and anus, as well as frequent infections in the oropharyngeal region. The molecular hallmarks of HPV42-induced carcinogenesis, including interactions with key tumour suppressor pathways and genomic integration, share striking similarities with high-risk HPV genotypes. This review synthesizes current evidence on the clinicopathological features, oncogenic mechanisms, epidemiological characteristics and diagnostic implications of HPV42-associated diseases. We also discuss the need for re-evaluating HPV42's risk classification and its implications for prevention and clinical management. A comprehensive understanding of HPV42's pathogenic spectrum is crucial for addressing the unmet clinical needs in diagnosing and treating its associated lesions and tumours.

analysis.summary_en: This review re-examines Human papillomavirus 42 (HPV42), traditionally classified as low-risk, by synthesizing evidence on its emerging oncogenic potential. HPV42 is now implicated in rare aggressive cutaneous tumours (digital papillary adenocarcinoma) and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions across cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal sites. Molecular analyses reveal similarities with high-risk HPV genotypes, including interactions with tumour suppressor pathways and genomic integration. However, uncertainties persist regarding HPV42's risk stratification, prevalence in diverse populations, and mechanistic contributions to oropharyngeal carcinogenesis. The review underscores the need for updated classification, targeted surveillance, and mechanistic research to address diagnostic and therapeutic gaps in HPV42-associated diseases.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了 人乳头瘤病毒 42 (HPV42),一种历史上被归类为低风险的基因型,重点关注其不断演变的致癌潜力和人类相关疾病。核心问题是,将 HPV42 的分子机制与 高危型HPV 基因型进行对比,是否应该对其进行重新分类,因为它与高级病变和罕见的侵袭性肿瘤有关。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了 HPV42 相关疾病的临床病理学、分子、流行病学和诊断证据,但没有指定数据库、检索日期、资格标准或选择方法。它整合了 HPV42 在数码乳头状腺癌、高级鳞状上皮内病变和口咽感染中作用的研究结果。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了 HPV42 风险分类的不确定性,以及需要进一步进行机制和流行病学研究以澄清其致癌驱动因素和疾病谱。关于 HPV42 的 患病率 在特定人群和地区的数据有限,并且其在口咽癌中作用的证据强度仍然不够充分。

title: Cervical human papillomavirus status among women with chronic inflammatory rheumatic diseases: matched cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Women with chronic inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and spondyloarthritis (SpA) are at increased risk for cervical precancer (CIN2+). It is unknown whether their human papillomavirus (HPV) status differs compared with a general screening population. Objectives To determine whether cervical screening reliant on HPV16/18 detection would be appropriate also in RA/SpA. Methods We included women with (1) RA (n = 53 816) or (2) SpA (n = 25 496) who were naïve to biologic-/targeted synthetic-disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARD), (3) women with RA (n = 14 033) or (4) SpA (n = 8297) starting a first b/tsDMARD, and matched (1:5) general population comparators, n = 504 290). Incident HPV infection was categorized as positive for HPV16/18, and/or other (non-16/18) HPV types. Relative risks (RRs) were assessed through log-binomial regression. Results Women with RA, whether exposed to b/tsDMARDs or not, had a higher prevalence of HPV (statistically significant RR of 1.17-1.18 vs comparators). Among women with SpA, risks were elevated in b/tsDMARD-exposed, as were other (non-16/18) HPV types. B/tsDMARD-naïve women with RA (but not those with bionaïve SpA) had higher risk for CIN2+ than comparators (RR = 1.20, 95% CI = 1.07 to 1.34). However, the proportion of women with CIN2+ positive for HPV16/18 or other HPV types did not differ vs comparators, neither in RA nor in SpA and whether b/tsDMARD-exposed or not. Conclusion Although some women with RA or SpA have higher risks for HPV and CIN2+ than the general population, their proportions of HPV16/18 vs other HPV types in CIN2+ do not differ. This is reassuring for cervical screening risk-stratifying women based on HPV16/18 detection.

title: [Prevalence of cervical human papillomavirus infection among women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China].
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical human papilloma virus (HPV) infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture of Yunnan Province to provide a theoretical basis for the strategy of cervical cancer prevention and treatment in this region. Methods: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled. The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution was analyzed and the disparities in infection patterns among different ethnic groups were compared. Results: The overall HPV prevalence among women in this region was 17.88% (2,254/12,605). Infections solely with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) predominated, with a prevalence of 14.75%, accounting for 82.48% (1,859/2,254) of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections exhibited a striking age-specific clustering among younger demographics; the prevalence in both the <20 and 20-29 years age groups reached 100%. The prevalence declined significantly with advancing age, dropping to 5.20% in the ≥60 years age group. Single-genotype infections constituted the primary pattern (74.00%, 1,668/2,254). However, multiple infections-particularly mixed infections of HR-HPV and low-risk HPV (LR-HPV)-were exceptionally prominent in the <20 years age group, peaking at 24.14%. Demographically, the overall HPV prevalence among ethnic minority women was significantly higher than that of Han women (23.14% vs. 15.62%, P<0.001), with the highest rates observed in the Dai (27.10%), Hani (26.30%), and Miao (25.17%) ethnicities. Although the general infection patterns (single vs. multiple) were similar between ethnicminority and Han women, ethnicminority women bore a significantly higher burden of specific HR-HPV types compared with Han women, including HPV-16 (3.56% vs. 1.92%), HPV-58 (3.03% vs. 1.58%), HPV-51 (2.45% vs. 1.24%), and HPV-59 (0.92% vs. 0.30%) (all P<0.05). Furthermore, inter-ethnic variations in genotype distribution were observed among the minority groups; notably, the distribution of HR-HPV-56 showed the most significant difference (P=0.018), with the highest prevalence found in women from the Dai ethnicity (3.74%). Conclusions: Cervical HPV infections among women in this region are predominantly driven by HR-HPV types 52, 16, and 58, exhibiting significant age and ethnic heterogeneity. Young women aged <30 years are highly susceptible not only to overall HPV infection, but also to mixed exposure involving multiple genotypes. Compared to Han women, ethnic minority women face a substantially more severe burden of HR-HPV infections. These findings suggest that future cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in this region should shift interventions to earlier stages, prioritizing early screening and health education for young women. Simultaneously, it is imperative to account for ethnic disparities, promote multivalent HPV vaccines that cover the predominant endemic strains, and develop targeted, precision-based prevention strategies tailored to specific ethnic regions.

abstract_original: Objective: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical human papilloma virus (HPV) infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture of Yunnan Province to provide a theoretical basis for the strategy of cervical cancer prevention and treatment in this region. Methods: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled. The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution was analyzed and the disparities in infection patterns among different ethnic groups were compared. Results: The overall HPV prevalence among women in this region was 17.88% (2,254/12,605). Infections solely with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) predominated, with a prevalence of 14.75%, accounting for 82.48% (1,859/2,254) of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections exhibited a striking age-specific clustering among younger demographics; the prevalence in both the <20 and 20-29 years age groups reached 100%. The prevalence declined significantly with advancing age, dropping to 5.20% in the ≥60 years age group. Single-genotype infections constituted the primary pattern (74.00%, 1,668/2,254). However, multiple infections-particularly mixed infections of HR-HPV and low-risk HPV (LR-HPV)-were exceptionally prominent in the <20 years age group, peaking at 24.14%. Demographically, the overall HPV prevalence among ethnic minority women was significantly higher than that of Han women (23.14% vs. 15.62%, P<0.001), with the highest rates observed in the Dai (27.10%), Hani (26.30%), and Miao (25.17%) ethnicities. Although the general infection patterns (single vs. multiple) were similar between ethnicminority and Han women, ethnicminority women bore a significantly higher burden of specific HR-HPV types compared with Han women, including HPV-16 (3.56% vs. 1.92%), HPV-58 (3.03% vs. 1.58%), HPV-51 (2.45% vs. 1.24%), and HPV-59 (0.92% vs. 0.30%) (all P<0.05). Furthermore, inter-ethnic variations in genotype distribution were observed among the minority groups; notably, the distribution of HR-HPV-56 showed the most significant difference (P=0.018), with the highest prevalence found in women from the Dai ethnicity (3.74%). Conclusions: Cervical HPV infections among women in this region are predominantly driven by HR-HPV types 52, 16, and 58, exhibiting significant age and ethnic heterogeneity. Young women aged <30 years are highly susceptible not only to overall HPV infection, but also to mixed exposure involving multiple genotypes. Compared to Han women, ethnic minority women face a substantially more severe burden of HR-HPV infections. These findings suggest that future cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in this region should shift interventions to earlier stages, prioritizing early screening and health education for young women. Simultaneously, it is imperative to account for ethnic disparities, promote multivalent HPV vaccines that cover the predominant endemic strains, and develop targeted, precision-based prevention strategies tailored to specific ethnic regions.

It enrolled 12,605 female residents across four medical centers between January 2018 and June 2024. The overall HPV prevalence was 17.88%, with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) infections predominating at 14.75%. The most common HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52, HPV-16, and HPV-58. abstract_zh: 【摘要】:目的:调查云南省红河哈尼族彝族自治州少数民族和汉族妇女宫颈人乳头状瘤病毒(HPV)感染情况及流行病学特征,为该地区制定宫颈癌预防策略和治疗提供理论依据。方法:连续纳入 2018 年 1 月至 2024 年 6 月期间在红河哈尼族彝族自治州四个医疗​​中心接受宫颈 HPV 基因分型的 12,605 名女性居民。分析HPV 患病率总体和基因型分布,并比较不同种族之间感染模式的差异。结果:该地区女性HPV 患病率总体感染率为17.88%(2,254/12,605)。仅感染 高危型HPV (HR-HPV) 为主,患病率 为 14.75%,占所有 HPV 阳性病例的 82.48% (1,859/2,254)。三种最常见的 HR-HPV 基因型是 HPV-52 (4.53%)、HPV-16 (2.41%) 和 HPV-58 (2.01%)。HPV 感染在年轻人群中表现出显着的年龄特异性聚集;<20岁和20-29岁年龄组的患病率均达到100%。患病率随着年龄的增长而显着下降,在≥60岁组中降至5.20%。单基因型感染构成主要模式(74.00%,1,668/2,254)。然而,多重感染,特别是HR-HPV和低危型HPV(LR-HPV)的混合感染,在<20岁年龄组中尤为突出,最高达到24.14%。从人口特征来看,少数民族女性HPV 患病率总体显着高于汉族女性(23.14% vs. 15.62%,P<0.001),其中傣族(27.10%)、哈尼族(26.30%)和苗族(25.17%)感染率最高。尽管少数民族和汉族女性的一般感染模式(单发与多发)相似,但与汉族女性相比,少数民族女性特定HR-HPV类型的负担明显更高,包括HPV-16(3.56% vs. 1.92%)、HPV-58(3.03% vs. 1.58%)、HPV-51(2.45% vs. 1.24%)和HPV-59 (0.92% vs. 0.30%)(均 P<0.05)。此外,在少数群体中观察到基因型分布的种族间差异;值得注意的是,HR-HPV-56的分布差异最为显着(P=0.018),其中患病率在傣族女性中最高(3.74%)。结论:该地区女性宫颈 HPV 感染主要由 HR-HPV 52、16 和 58 型驱动,表现出显着的年龄和种族异质性。年龄<30岁的年轻女性不仅对整体HPV感染高度敏感,而且对涉及多种基因型的混合暴露也高度敏感。与汉族女性相比,少数民族女性面临着更严重的HR-HPV感染负担。这些结果表明,该地区未来的宫颈癌防控策略应将干预措施转向早期阶段,优先考虑对年轻女性的早期筛查和健康教育。同时,要考虑民族差异,推广涵盖优势流行毒株的多价HPV 疫苗,并针对特定民族地区制定有针对性、精准化的预防策略。

title: Evaluating the Impact of an Educational Intervention on Medical Students’ Knowledge and Attitudes Toward Human Papillomavirus
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant public health concern due to its rising incidence and strong association with cancers of the head, neck, and genitalia. High-risk HPV types are responsible for cervical, oropharyngeal, and various anogenital cancers. Despite proven vaccine efficacy, vaccination rates remain low in adolescents and young adults. This study assessed whether an educational infographic improved medical students' knowledge and attitudes toward HPV. Medical students (years 1-4) at Wayne State University completed electronic pre- and post-intervention surveys regarding an infographic covering HPV, HPV-related cancers, and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) vaccination guidelines. Surveys included demographic questions and pre- and post-infographic items assessing HPV knowledge and attitudes using a Likert-scale format. 234 paired responses were analyzed using paired t-tests. Students demonstrated significant post-intervention increases in knowledge of HPV types (p < 0.001), transmissibility (p < 0.001), vaccination schedule (p < 0.001), and side effects (p < 0.001). Likelihood of encouraging vaccination to family members within three months increased (p < 0.001). title: Improving Cervical Cancer Screening Participation Through Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling: A Scoping Review of Evidence in Underserved Populations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer remains the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, with an estimated 660,000 new cases and 348,000 deaths in 2022. Despite the demonstrated efficacy of established screening programs, participation remains disproportionately low in underserved populations due to structural, cultural, and personal barriers. Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling has emerged as a promising strategy to improve access to cervical cancer screening for these groups. OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesize evidence on the acceptability and implementation of HPV self-sampling for cervical cancer screening among marginalized populations. METHODS: A scoping review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines was conducted. PubMed and Embase were searched for literature published between 2002 and 2025. Studies were eligible if they reported acceptability, feasibility, or participant preferences for HPV self-sampling in at least one defined marginalized population. Data were synthesized narratively. Restriction to two databases is acknowledged as a methodological limitation. RESULTS: Ten studies spanning eight countries and involving over 6400 participants were included. Acceptance rates ranged from 21% to 98%. Higher acceptance was consistently associated with community-driven implementation models incorporating community health worker involvement, culturally tailored education, and home-visit options. Privacy, autonomy, and convenience were key facilitators; low literacy, fear of results, and health care mistrust were the most common barriers. CONCLUSIONS: HPV self-sampling can achieve high acceptance in marginalized communities when implemented through culturally sensitive, community-engaged programs with adequate support infrastructure. Integrating education, navigation support, and low-barrier follow-up care offers significant potential for advancing health equity in cervical cancer prevention.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV) and HPV-associated cervical cancer screening in underserved populations, focusing on the acceptability and implementation of HPV self-sampling as an intervention to improve participation in cervical cancer prevention programs.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching PubMed and Embase for literature published between 2002 and 2025. Eligible studies reported acceptability, feasibility, or participant preferences for HPV self-sampling in marginalized populations, with data synthesized narratively. Ten studies across eight countries involving over 6400 participants were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV self-sampling achieves high acceptance rates (21% to 98%) in marginalized communities when implemented through culturally sensitive, community-engaged programs. Key facilitators include privacy, autonomy, and convenience, while barriers encompass low literacy, fear of results, and healthcare mistrust.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges methodological limitations, including restriction to two databases and reliance on narrative synthesis without pooled estimates. Evidence gaps persist regarding long-term outcomes, optimal implementation strategies across diverse settings, and the impact of self-sampling on follow-up care adherence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrating culturally tailored education, community health worker involvement, and low-barrier follow-up care is critical to advance health equity in cervical cancer prevention. Future research should prioritize comparative effectiveness studies and implementation science to optimize self-sampling programs in underserved populations.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates HPV self-sampling as a strategy to improve cervical cancer screening participation among underserved populations. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it synthesizes evidence from ten studies across eight countries involving over 6400 participants, highlighting high acceptance rates (21%–98%) when programs are culturally sensitive and community-engaged. Facilitators include privacy, autonomy, and convenience, while barriers such as low literacy, fear of results, and healthcare mistrust persist. Methodological limitations include reliance on two databases and narrative synthesis without pooled estimates. The review concludes that integrating education, navigation support, and accessible follow-up care can advance health equity, while calling for comparative effectiveness research and implementation science to address evidence gaps.

title_zh: 通过 人乳头瘤病毒 自我抽样提高 宫颈癌 筛查参与:对服务不足人群证据的范围界定审查。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer remains the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, with an estimated 660,000 new cases and 348,000 deaths in 2022. Despite the demonstrated efficacy of established screening programs, participation remains disproportionately low in underserved populations due to structural, cultural, and personal barriers. Human papillomavirus (HPV) self-sampling has emerged as a promising strategy to improve access to cervical cancer screening for these groups. OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesize evidence on the acceptability and implementation of HPV self-sampling for cervical cancer screening among marginalized populations. METHODS: A scoping review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines was conducted. PubMed and Embase were searched for literature published between 2002 and 2025. Studies were eligible if they reported acceptability, feasibility, or participant preferences for HPV self-sampling in at least one defined marginalized population. Data were synthesized narratively. Restriction to two databases is acknowledged as a methodological limitation. RESULTS: Ten studies spanning eight countries and involving over 6400 participants were included. Acceptance rates ranged from 21% to 98%. Higher acceptance was consistently associated with community-driven implementation models incorporating community health worker involvement, culturally tailored education, and home-visit options. Privacy, autonomy, and convenience were key facilitators; low literacy, fear of results, and health care mistrust were the most common barriers. CONCLUSIONS: HPV self-sampling can achieve high acceptance in marginalized communities when implemented through culturally sensitive, community-engaged programs with adequate support infrastructure. Integrating education, navigation support, and low-barrier follow-up care offers significant potential for advancing health equity in cervical cancer prevention.
abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌 仍然是全球女性中第四大常见癌症,预计到 2022 年将有 660,000 例新病例和 348,000 例死亡。尽管现有筛查计划已被证明有效,但由于结构、文化和个人障碍,在服务不足的人群中,参与率仍然不成比例地低。人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 自我采样已成为一种有前景的策略,可改善这些群体获得 宫颈癌 筛查的机会。目的:绘制并综合证据,说明在边缘化人群中进行 HPV 自我采样以进行 宫颈癌 筛查的可接受性和实施情况。方法:按照系统评价的首选报告项目和范围界定审查指南的荟萃分析扩展进行了范围界定审查。PubMed 和 Embase 检索了 2002 年至 2025 年间发表的文献。如果研究报告了至少一个确定的边缘化人群中 HPV 自我采样的可接受性、可行性或参与者偏好,则研究合格。数据以叙述方式综合。对两个数据库的限制被认为是方法上的限制。结果:纳入了涵盖 8 个国家、涉及 6400 多名参与者的 10 项研究。录取率从 21% 到 98% 不等。更高的接受度始终与社区驱动的实施模式相关,其中包括社区卫生工作者的参与、文化定制教育和家访选择。隐私、自主和便利是关键的促进因素;识字率低、对结果的恐惧以及对医疗保健的不信任是最常见的障碍。结论:当通过文化敏感、社区参与的计划和足够的支持基础设施实施时,HPV 自我采样可以在边缘化社区获得高度接受。将教育、导航支持和低门槛后续护理相结合,为促进 宫颈癌 预防的健康公平提供了巨大潜力。

title: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' Exploring the acceptability of future Human Papillomavirus self-sampling, and the barriers and facilitators of cervical cancer screening for those with intellectual disabilities in Scotland.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening attendance among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland is approximately 30%, significantly below the general population rate of 69% and the WHO's recommended 70% target. HPV self-sampling could provide a more accessible screening option for this underserved population. This study aimed to understand the views and experiences of women with ID regarding cervical cancer screening and the acceptability of HPV self-sampling. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID who attended third-sector community groups across Scotland, along with their carers. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, with a total of 13 participants (11 women with ID, 2 carers). Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged: (1) National Health Service (NHS) communication as a source of distress; (2) power imbalances between health care providers and women with ID: feeling unheard, dismissed and out of control; (3) enduring consequences of inadequate care; (4) past trauma shapes future avoidance; and (5) self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening. CONCLUSION: This research reveals significant systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID, whilst highlighting self-sampling's transformative potential. Successful implementation requires comprehensive accessible information, enhanced health care professional training and trauma-informed care approaches. Self-sampling could significantly advance health equity goals whilst improving health care outcomes for this underserved population.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 苏格兰智障女性 (ID) 参加 宫颈癌 筛查的比例约为 30%,远低于总人口 69% 的比例和世界卫生组织 70% 的目标。该研究旨在探索筛查的障碍和促进因素,并评估未来 HPV 自我采样作为这一服务不足群体更容易获得的选择的可接受性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 通过焦点小组对苏格兰各地的智障女性及其护理人员进行了一项定性研究。2024 年 9 月至 10 月期间举办了四次焦点小组,涉及 13 名参与者(11 名患有智障的女性和 2 名护理人员)。
elements_zh.methods: 通过焦点小组收集数据,并使用反思性主题分析进行分析,以确定与筛查经验和自我抽样可接受性相关的关键主题。
elements_zh.main_results: 出现了五个主题:NHS 沟通是痛苦的根源;医疗保健提供者和智障女性之间的权力失衡;护理不足造成的持久后果;过去的创伤塑造了未来的回避;自我抽样作为赋权的途径。参与者表现出对自我采样的高度接受度,将其视为克服传统筛查障碍的潜在解决方案。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调了当前针对智障女性的 宫颈癌 筛查服务存在系统性不足,同时将自我采样确定为一种变革性的潜在解决方案。新颖之处在于集中智障女性的声音来揭示未满足的需求并提出可行的改变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过解决 宫颈癌 筛查项目中的准入障碍和创伤知情护理差距,自我采样可以推进健康公平目标并改善患有智力障碍的女性的医疗保健结果。

The study sought to explore barriers and facilitators to screening and to assess the acceptability of future HPV self-sampling as a more accessible option for this underserved group.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID and their carers across Scotland. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, involving 13 participants (11 women with ID and 2 carers).
analysis_en.methods: Data were collected through focus groups and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis to identify key themes related to screening experiences and self-sampling acceptability.
analysis_en.main_results: Five main themes emerged: NHS communication as a source of distress; power imbalances between healthcare providers and women with ID; enduring consequences of inadequate care; past trauma shaping future avoidance; and self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The research highlights systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID while identifying self-sampling as a transformative potential solution. The novelty lies in centring the voices of women with ID to reveal unmet needs and propose actionable changes.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Self-sampling could advance health equity goals and improve healthcare outcomes for women with ID by addressing access barriers and trauma-informed care gaps in cervical cancer screening programs.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The qualitative design limits generalisability, and the small sample size (n=13) may not capture the full diversity of experiences among women with ID. Evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of quantitative validation and reliance on self-reported perspectives.

title_zh: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' 探讨未来人乳头瘤病毒自我采样的可接受性,以及苏格兰智力障碍人群进行宫颈癌筛查的障碍与促进因素
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening attendance among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland is approximately 30%, significantly below the general population rate of 69% and the WHO's recommended 70% target. HPV self-sampling could provide a more accessible screening option for this underserved population. This study aimed to understand the views and experiences of women with ID regarding cervical cancer screening and the acceptability of HPV self-sampling. METHODS: A qualitative study using focus groups was conducted with women with ID who attended third-sector community groups across Scotland, along with their carers. Four focus groups were held between September and October 2024, with a total of 13 participants (11 women with ID, 2 carers). Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged: (1) National Health Service (NHS) communication as a source of distress; (2) power imbalances between health care providers and women with ID: feeling unheard, dismissed and out of control; (3) enduring consequences of inadequate care; (4) past trauma shapes future avoidance; and (5) self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. Participants demonstrated high acceptability of self-sampling, viewing it as a potential solution to overcome barriers to traditional screening. CONCLUSION: This research reveals significant systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID, whilst highlighting self-sampling's transformative potential. Successful implementation requires comprehensive accessible information, enhanced health care professional training and trauma-informed care approaches. Self-sampling could significantly advance health equity goals whilst improving health care outcomes for this underserved population.
abstract_zh: 背景:苏格兰智障女性 (ID) 的 宫颈癌 筛查出勤率约为 30%,远低于总人口 69% 的比率和世界卫生组织建议的 70% 目标。HPV 自我采样可以为这一服务不足的人群提供更方便的筛查选择。本研究旨在了解患有 ID 的女性对 宫颈癌 筛查以及 HPV 自我采样的可接受性的看法和经验。方法:利用焦点小组对参与苏格兰第三部门社区团体的智障女性及其护理人员进行了一项定性研究。2024 年 9 月至 10 月期间举办了四次焦点小组,共有 13 名参与者(11 名患有智力障碍的女性,2 名护理人员)。使用反思性主题分析对数据进行分析。结果:出现了五个主题:(1) 国家卫生服务 (NHS) 沟通是痛苦的根源;(2) 医疗保健提供者和智障妇女之间的权力失衡:感觉被忽视、被忽视和失控;(3) 护理不足造成的持久后果;(4)过去的创伤塑造了未来的回避;(5) 自我抽样作为赋权的途径。参与者表现出对自我采样的高度接受度,将其视为克服传统筛查障碍的潜在解决方案。结论:这项研究揭示了当前 宫颈癌 针对 ID 女性的筛查服务存在显着的系统性缺陷,同时强调了自我采样的变革潜力。成功的实施需要全面的可获取信息、加强的医疗保健专业培训和创伤知情护理方法。自我采样可以显着推进健康公平目标,同时改善这一服务不足人群的医疗保健结果。

title: Awareness and Acceptance of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine and Associated Factors Among Parents of Adolescents (9-18 Years) at a Children's Hospital in Babol, Iran: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a major cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers, and vaccination is an effective preventive strategy when administered during adolescence. Because parental decision-making plays a central role in adolescent vaccination uptake, this cross-sectional study aimed to assess parental awareness, attitudes, and barriers related to HPV infection and HPV vaccination, as well as demographic factors associated with vaccine awareness, among parents of adolescents attending a tertiary pediatric hospital in Babol, Iran. METHODS: In this cross-sectional survey, 300 parents of children aged 9-18 years who attended inpatient wards or outpatient clinics at Shafizadeh Children's Hospital were consecutively recruited. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing demographic characteristics, awareness of HPV and HPV vaccination, attitudes toward vaccination, and perceived barriers and motivators. Associations between parental awareness of HPV vaccination and demographic variables were analyzed using chi-square tests, independent-samples t-tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests, as appropriate. RESULTS: Awareness of HPV infection and HPV vaccination was reported by 43.7% and 38.3% of parents, respectively, while only 14.7% correctly identified the recommended age for vaccination. HPV vaccination uptake was very low; only 4 parents (1.3%) had received the vaccine themselves, and 2 (0.7%) had vaccinated their children. Although 52.7% of parents were classified as having a favorable attitude toward HPV vaccination, 96.7% cited high cost and 34.0% limited availability as major barriers. Knowledge of HPV vaccination was significantly higher among parents who were younger, had a university education, resided in urban areas, worked in medical or professional occupations, and had higher household income (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Parental awareness of HPV vaccination and actual vaccine uptake were low despite generally favorable attitudes. Structural barriers, particularly high cost and limited availability, appear to be major factors linked to poor uptake. Integrating HPV vaccination into national immunization programs, improving insurance coverage, and implementing targeted educational interventions may increase vaccination rates among Iranian adolescents.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of low adolescent HPV vaccination uptake by examining why parental awareness and acceptance of HPV vaccination remain insufficient despite its proven role in preventing HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 300 parents of adolescents aged 9–18 years attending inpatient or outpatient services at Shafizadeh Children’s Hospital in Babol, Iran.
analysis.methods: Parents completed a structured questionnaire capturing demographic characteristics, awareness of HPV and HPV vaccination, attitudes toward vaccination, and perceived barriers and motivators.
analysis.main_results: Awareness of HPV infection and HPV vaccination was reported by 43.7% and 38.3% of parents, respectively, while only 14.7% correctly identified the recommended vaccination age; HPV vaccination uptake was very low, with only 4 parents (1.3%) vaccinated themselves and 2 (0.7%) having vaccinated their children.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that despite generally favorable attitudes (52.7%), structural barriers such as high cost (96.7%) and limited availability (34.0%) largely explain the low uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that integrating HPV vaccination into national immunization programs, improving insurance coverage, and implementing targeted educational interventions could increase vaccination rates among Iranian adolescents.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre, cross-sectional design limits generalisability, and reliance on self-reported awareness and uptake may introduce reporting bias, warranting a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Babol, Iran assessed parental awareness, attitudes, and barriers regarding HPV infection and HPV vaccination among 300 parents of adolescents aged 9–18 years. Awareness of HPV infection and vaccination was low (43.7% and 38.3%, respectively), with only 14.7% correctly identifying the recommended vaccination age. Despite 52.7% of parents holding favorable attitudes, HPV vaccination uptake was extremely low (1.3% among parents and 0.7% among children). Structural barriers, particularly high cost (96.7%) and limited availability (34.0%), were cited as major impediments. The authors propose integrating HPV vaccination into national programs, enhancing insurance coverage, and delivering targeted education to improve uptake.

elements_zh.main_results: 分别有 43.7% 和 38.3% 的家长报告对 HPV 感染和 HPV 疫苗接种 的了解,而只有 14.7% 的家长正确识别了推荐的 疫苗接种 年龄;HPV 疫苗接种 的接种率非常低,只有 4 名家长 (1.3%) 自己接种了疫苗,2 名家长 (0.7%) 为孩子接种了疫苗。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将调查结果解读为,尽管普遍持积极态度(52.7%),但高成本(96.7%)和有限可用性(34.0%)等结构性障碍在很大程度上解释了采用率低的原因。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,将 HPV 疫苗接种 纳入国家免疫计划、提高保险覆盖范围和实施有针对性的教育干预措施可以提高伊朗青少年的 疫苗接种 率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 单中心、横截面设计限制了普遍性,并且依赖自我报告的认知和吸收可能会引入报告偏差,需要中等强度的证据。

title: Integrative analysis of the m6A epitranscriptome in HeLa-expressed HPV18 early transcripts reveals its potential impact on splicing.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cancers remain a major global health burden, and understanding how posttranscriptional regulation shapes viral gene expression may inform new therapeutic strategies. Here, we reanalyzed independently generated public HeLa data sets to identify candidate RNA modification sites on integrated HPV18 transcripts expressed from the HeLa genome. Using Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing of native RNAs and in vitro transcribed controls, together with GLORI, eTAM-seq and staged 4sU-GLORI data sets, we identified a set of candidate m6A sites on HPV18 early transcripts. m6A levels at a subset of these sites were reduced following perturbation of the m6A pathway, most clearly after METTL3 inhibition, WTAP knockdown, or FTO overexpression. We further show that the E6*I-proximal m6A site at position 224 is enriched on unspliced transcripts in direct RNA sequencing, as supported by several of the analyzed data sets. In contrast, we find no convincing evidence for m5C or pseudouridine within the HPV18 regions covered by these data sets. Together, our analyses provide a candidate map of RNA modifications on HeLa-expressed HPV18 early transcripts.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the m6A epitranscriptome of HPV18 early transcripts expressed in HeLa cells, aiming to understand how posttranscriptional regulation influences viral gene expression. The researchers reanalyzed public HeLa datasets using Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing and complementary methods to identify candidate m6A modification sites. They found that m6A levels at certain sites decreased when the m6A pathway was perturbed, with the E6*I-proximal site at position 224 showing enrichment on unspliced transcripts. These findings suggest potential roles for m6A in HPV18 transcript splicing and may inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the study does not report limitations or evidence strength, which could affect the confidence in these results. The research contributes to the understanding of RNA modifications in HPV-related cancers and highlights the need for further investigation into their functional implications.

title: The Antiviral Activity of Sandalwood Oil on Human Papillomavirus Type 16 Using a Disc-Based Carrier Assay
abstract: Essential oils derived from plants have gained increasing interest in recent years for their potential antimicrobial, antiviral, and disinfectant properties. However, data specifically examining the virucidal efficacy of essential oils against human papillomavirus (HPV), a major human pathogen, remains very limited. In this study, we compared the chemical composition of sandalwood essential oils derived from five different species (Santalum album, S. austrocaledonicum, S. We further investigated the ability of S. album sandalwood oil, the species highest in α- and β-santalol content, to inactivate infectious HPV type 16 virions dried onto glass carriers at contact times of 5 and 30 min. HPV-16 is a high-risk HPV type frequently associated with cervical and other cancers. A RT-qPCR assay based on E1^E4 spliced transcript detection was used to measure viral infectivity levels post-treatment. album oil exhibited moderate but incomplete virucidal activity, achieving a mean 2.59 log reduction (99.7% inactivation) of HPV-16 after a 30 min contact time. In contrast, the shorter 5 min contact time resulted in negligible reductions in viral infectivity compared to untreated controls. These data suggest that while S. album oil has the ability to inactivate HPV, it requires relatively long contact times to achieve significant reduction.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Despite growing interest in essential oils for antimicrobial and antiviral applications, data on their efficacy against human papillomavirus (HPV), a major human pathogen, remain scarce.

analysis.methods: Infectivity was measured using an RT-qPCR assay targeting the E1^E4 spliced transcript to quantify viral RNA levels after treatment with Santalum album oil at contact times of 5 and 30 minutes.
analysis.main_results: Santalum album oil achieved a mean 2.59 log reduction (99.7% inactivation) of HPV-16 after 30 minutes, whereas a 5-minute contact time produced negligible reductions compared to untreated controls.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that Santalum album oil exhibits moderate but incomplete virucidal activity against HPV-16, requiring prolonged contact times for significant inactivation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest potential for sandalwood oil as a supplementary disinfectant against HPV-16 in settings where prolonged contact can be ensured, though clinical applicability remains untested.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its in vitro design, lack of clinical validation, and reliance on a single HPV type, which constrains generalizability and reduces confidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the virucidal activity of Santalum album sandalwood oil against human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) using a disc-based carrier assay with dried virions on glass carriers. The authors measured infectivity via RT-qPCR targeting the E1^E4 spliced transcript after treatment at 5- and 30-minute contact times. Santalum album oil achieved a mean 2.59 log reduction (99.7% inactivation) after 30 minutes, while a 5-minute exposure showed negligible effects. The authors interpret these results as demonstrating moderate but incomplete virucidal activity requiring prolonged contact. The findings imply potential for sandalwood oil as a supplementary disinfectant in controlled settings, though clinical applicability is untested. The study’s in vitro design, focus on a single HPV type, and absence of clinical validation limit generalizability and reduce confidence to moderate.

title: Effect of thermal ablation on persistent HPV infection in Danish women ≥ 40 years of age: a quasi-randomized clinical study
abstract: Thermal ablation is a cervical heat treatment that destroys a defined area of the cervix. We evaluated whether thermal ablation facilitates HPV clearance in women with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection, using HPV status and FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA methylation as molecular markers for treatment efficacy. A total of 131 women aged ≥ 40 years with persistent HR-HPV infection but without histologically confirmed high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (≥ CIN2) were enrolled at three outpatient gynecological clinics. After exclusions, 39 women were allocated to the intervention arm (thermal ablation) and 34 to the no treatment only control arm. Allocation was based on date of birth (even dates: intervention; odd dates: control), using quasi-randomization. HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status were assessed at baseline (0 months), 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using the WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 min and at 100 °C for 40 s, administered across two sessions 2–3 days apart. At 10 months, 64.1% of women in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive. No significant difference in HPV positivity was observed between arms at any time point. FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation positivity showed a transient decrease in the intervention arm (-10.2%) at 3 months but increased in both arms over 10 months to above baseline levels, with no significant treatment effect. Thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance in women with persistent HR-HPV infection without significant cervical disease. Methylation positivity increased over time in both study arms, consistent with ongoing oncogenic transformation. Women treated with thermal ablation remain HR-HPV positive and require continued surveillance, indicating no clinical benefit over observation alone. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07376031, registered 21 January 2026. Thermal ablation does not significantly affect HPV clearance or FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status in women ≥40 years with persistent high-risk HPV infection without significant cervical disease.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管没有高级别病变,但年龄≥40岁的女性持续高危人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV)感染仍存在进展为宫颈疾病的风险。该研究旨在利用 HPV 状态和 FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA 甲基化作为 治疗 功效的分子标记,确定热消融是否有助于该人群的 HPV 清除。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项半随机临床研究在三个妇科门诊招募了 131 名年龄≥40 岁、持续 HR-HPV 感染但无组织学证实的高级别宫颈上皮内瘤变 (≥CIN2) 的女性。排除后,39 名女性被分配到热消融组,34 名女性被分配到非 治疗 对照组,使用基于出生日期的准随机化。
elements_zh.methods: 在基线、3 个月和 10 个月时评估 HPV 基因分型和 FAM19A4/miR124-2 甲基化状态。使用 WISAP 探头在 65 °C 下进行热消融 2 分钟,在 100 °C 下进行 40 秒,分两次进行,间隔 2-3 天。
elements_zh.main_results: 10 个月时,干预组中 64.1% 的女性和对照组中 79.4% 的女性仍保持 HR-HPV 阳性,两组之间在任何时间点都没有显着差异。FAM19A4/miR124-2 甲基化阳性率在 3 个月时在干预组中显示短暂下降 (-10.2%),但在 10 个月后两组中均增加至基线水平以上,但没有显着的 治疗 效应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,对于持续性 HR-HPV 感染但无明显宫颈疾病的女性,热消融不会促进 HPV 清除或降低致癌转化风险,正如双臂持续 HPV 阳性和甲基化阳性增加所证明的那样。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对于该人群中的 HPV 清除,热消融并没有比单独观察提供临床益处,这表明持续的 监测 仍然是必要的,并且应探索针对 ≥ 40 岁女性持续性 HR-HPV 感染的替代策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的准随机设计和缺乏对高级病变的组织学确认限制了因果推断和普遍性。由于样本量小、未实施盲法以及依赖分子标志物而不是临床终点,证据强度中等。

title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination programmes across European countries: time-harmonized coverage among adolescent females, socioeconomic predictors, and impact on public interest
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination represents a cornerstone of cervical cancer prevention and is essential to achieving the WHO elimination targets in Europe. The study aimed to assess HPV vaccination coverage trends among adolescent females across Europe, identify key predictors of uptake, and evaluate the association between the introduction of HPV vaccination into National Immunization Programmes (NIPs) and public interest, as reflected by online search activity. METHODS: This country-level longitudinal study analysed available 2010-2023 full-dose HPV vaccination coverage data among 15-year-old females across 43 European countries, by years since introduction within the NIPs. Socioeconomic, institutional, health-system, and delivery indicators were integrated with Google Trends Relative Search Volume for the "HPV vaccine" topic. Multivariable GEE models were used to identify predictors of vaccination coverage, while Pearson correlations assessed the association between Relative Search Volume and coverage. RESULTS: Coverage among adolescent females increased markedly after NIP introduction, with population-weighted coverage reaching about 40% by year 2 and stabilising at 55-60% by year 5. Coverage exceeded 60% in most countries by year 15. Multivariable analyses identified lower public disagreement with vaccine safety and higher physician density as significant determinants, with interactions between time since NIP introduction and HDI. School-based programmes were associated with a faster increase. Among 32 countries with Google Trends data, 53% showed significant Relative Search Volume changes after NIP introduction, and Relative Search Volume strongly correlated with coverage (r = 0.89). CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination coverage among adolescent females in Europe remains uneven and below the WHO 90% target. Strengthening public confidence, primary care capacity, school-based delivery, and digital monitoring may help close immunization gaps and accelerate progress toward cervical cancer elimination.

title: Effects of School-Entry Vaccination Mandates on Adolescent Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Uptake: United States, 2008-2023.
abstract: To evaluate the association between school-entry vaccination mandates and adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination uptake in the United States. We conducted a quasi-experimental study using a difference-in-differences approach comparing HPV vaccination uptake (≥ 1 dose) in mandate (n = 4) versus nonmandate (n = 47) states and territories by sex. We used provider-verified vaccination records from the 2008-2023 National Immunization Survey-Teen (n = 240 616) for adolescents aged 13 to 17 years. Models accounted for staggered policy implementation and adjusted for demographic and socioeconomic covariates. School-entry mandates were associated with 6.4 percentage-points (95% confidence interval [CI] = 3.6, 9.1) higher HPV vaccination uptake among girls and 3.4 percentage points (95% CI = 1.8, 5.0) higher uptake among boys. Associations with HPV vaccination uptake increased over time for girls, whereas for boys, associations were concentrated in the first few years following implementation and attenuated thereafter. School-entry mandates are associated with higher HPV vaccination uptake among adolescents. Public Health Implications. Although mandates alone are unlikely to achieve national HPV vaccination targets, they may serve as an important component of comprehensive state efforts to increase uptake and prevent HPV-related cancers. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print August 20, 2026:e1-e4. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308635).

title: HPV16 Genomic Status Stratifies Risk of Disease Recurrence in Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Purpose: A subset of patients with human papillomavirus (HPV)–positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) develops disease recurrence despite generally favorable outcomes. Reliable biomarkers for risk stratification remain lacking. We investigated whether comprehensive viral genomic profiling refines prognostic classification. Experimental Design: Tumor samples from 100 patients with p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC enrolled in 2 independent cohorts were analyzed using targeted viral capture sequencing. Viral genotype, sublineage, single-nucleotide variation, virus–host integration sites, viral structural variants (SV), clonality, and viral copy number were characterized. Associations with cumulative incidence of progression, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival were assessed at 60 months. Results: HPV16 was detected in 94 tumors, 83 of which belonged to the HPV16_A1 sublineage. Within this sublineage, 20 tumors harbored strictly episomal viral genomes, whereas 63 exhibited integration and/or viral SV. No progression events occurred in the strictly episomal HPV16_A1 subgroup, whereas 12 occurred among HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. At 60 months, no progression events were observed in strictly episomal HPV16_A1 tumors compared with a 23.1% cumulative incidence of progression in HPV16_A1 tumors with an integration and/or SV. Previously reported high-risk single-nucleotide variants and a novel upstream regulatory region variant were associated with worse PFS. Integration sites were enriched in open chromatin and promoter regions and clustered within viral E2 and E4 genes. Conclusions: Within HPV16_A1 tumors, viral genomic architecture defines clinically distinct subgroups. Strictly episomal (wild-type) genomes identify a low-risk population, whereas integration and SV characterize higher-risk disease.

Tumor samples from 100 p16-positive and HPV DNA–positive OPSCC patients across two cohorts underwent targeted viral capture sequencing to characterize HPV16 genotype, sublineage, mutations, integration sites, structural variants, clonality, and viral copy number. abstract_zh: 摘要 目的:尽管预后总体良好,但 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 阳性口咽鳞状细胞癌 (OPSCC) 患者的一部分仍会出现疾病复发。仍然缺乏用于风险分层的可靠生物标志物。我们研究了全面的病毒基因组分析是否可以改善预后分类。实验设计:使用靶向病毒捕获测序对参加 2 个独立 队列研究 的 100 名 p16 阳性和 HPV DNA 阳性 OPSCC 患者的肿瘤样本进行分析。对病毒基因型、亚系、单核苷酸变异、病毒-宿主整合位点、病毒结构变异(SV)、克隆性和病毒拷贝数进行了表征。在 60 个月时评估与累积 发病率 进展、无进展生存期 (PFS) 和总生存期的关联。结果:94个肿瘤中检测到HPV16,其中83个属于HPV16_A1亚系。在该亚系中,20 个肿瘤具有严格附加型病毒 基因组,而 63 个则表现出整合和/或病毒 SV。在严格附加型 HPV16_A1 亚组中没有发生进展事件,而在具有整合和/或 SV 的 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中发生了 12 起进展事件。60 个月时,在严格附加型 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中没有观察到进展事件,而在具有整合和/或 SV 的 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中,累积进展 发病率 为 23.1%。先前报道的高风险单核苷酸变异和新型上游调控区变异与较差的 PFS 相关。整合位点在开放染色质和启动子区域富集,并聚集在病毒 E2 和 E4 基因内。结论:在 HPV16_A1 肿瘤中,病毒基因组结构定义了临床上不同的亚组。严格附加型(野生型)基因组 识别低风险人群,而整合和 SV 则表征高风险疾病。
