title: Exploration of immune correlates of viral clearance after PVX2 immunotherapy in patients with human papillomavirus type 16 infection and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade ≤1
abstract: ABSTRACT Immune responses correlated with clearance of human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) were sought in PVX2 immunotherapy-treated CIN ≤1 patients. PVX2 comprises intramuscular vaccinations with HPV16 E7-targeted pNGVL4a-Sig/E7(detox)/HSP70 DNA vaccine (3 mg, weeks 0 and 4) and HPV16 L2E7E6 fusion protein (TA-CIN; 100 μg week 8). Administering PVX2 to 12 women with HPV16+ CIN ≤1 elicited both antibody and CD8+ T-cell responses, including changes in TCR diversity, clonal expansion, and emergence of public clonotypes. HPV16 was not detected in 5/11 evaluable participants at month 6. Post-vaccination E6, E7, and L2-specific antibody titers were higher, but none correlated with clearance. Neither TCR clonal diversity/expansion nor public clonotypes were associated with HPV16 clearance. While the fractions of expanded/new clonotypes were not associated with HPV16 clearance, a higher proportion of vaccine antigen-specific reads was evident post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. High baseline serum MCP-1 associated with HPV16 persistence, and MIP-1β trended higher post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. IMPORTANCE HPV16 is a necessary cause of over half of all cervical cancers, and in even higher fractions of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Treatments for HPV16 infection and associated pre-cancerous lesions are needed given the disease burden and limitations of current treatments. Women with persistent HPV infections endure anxiety and stress due to frequent colposcopies, inconvenience, healthcare costs from active surveillance, and potential to transmit the virus to other sexual partners. Since a majority of patients can spontaneously clear their infections, administration of an immunotherapy may promote the elimination of otherwise persistent infections where disease can progress.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) infection is a necessary cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers, yet many infections clear spontaneously, creating a need for immunotherapies that safely promote viral clearance in persistent cases. The study aimed to identify immune correlates associated with HPV16 clearance following PVX2 immunotherapy in women with HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade ≤1.
analysis.study_design_and_population: PVX2 immunotherapy was administered to 12 women with HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade ≤1 in a clinical setting, with immune responses assessed over time to evaluate correlates of viral clearance.
analysis.methods: PVX2 consisted of intramuscular HPV16 E7-targeted pNGVL4a-Sig/E7(detox)/HSP70 DNA vaccine (3 mg at weeks 0 and 4) followed by HPV16 L2E7E6 fusion protein (TA-CIN; 100 μg at week 8), with post-vaccination immune profiling including antibody titers, CD8+ T-cell responses, TCR diversity, and cytokine measurements.
analysis.main_results: HPV16 was not detected in 5 of 11 evaluable participants at month 6, while post-vaccination E6, E7, and L2-specific antibody titers were higher but did not correlate with clearance. Neither TCR clonal diversity/expansion nor public clonotypes were associated with HPV16 clearance, though a higher proportion of vaccine antigen-specific reads was observed post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that antibody titers and TCR repertoire changes alone did not predict HPV16 clearance, suggesting that vaccine antigen-specific immune responses may be more relevant than global TCR metrics. They highlighted the emergence of vaccine antigen-specific reads as a potential novel correlate warranting further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings cautiously suggest that PVX2 immunotherapy may promote HPV16 clearance in some women with low-grade lesions, potentially reducing the need for invasive surveillance and associated healthcare burdens, though correlates of protection remain incompletely defined.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s small sample size (n=12) and lack of a control group limit causal inference and generalizability, and reliance on abstract-only evidence further constrains the strength of conclusions regarding immune correlates of clearance.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated immune correlates of HPV16 clearance after PVX2 immunotherapy in 12 women with HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade ≤1. PVX2 combined an HPV16 E7-targeted DNA vaccine with a fusion protein, eliciting antibody and CD8+ T-cell responses. At month 6, HPV16 was undetectable in 5 of 11 evaluable participants. Post-vaccination antibody titers to E6, E7, and L2 were elevated but did not correlate with clearance. TCR repertoire metrics, including diversity and public clonotypes, were not associated with clearance, though vaccine antigen-specific reads were higher in those clearing HPV16. Baseline serum MCP-1 associated with HPV16 persistence, while MIP-1β trended higher post-vaccination in those clearing HPV16. The small sample size and absence of a control group limit the strength of conclusions, and correlates of protection remain uncertain.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 持续性 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 (HPV16) 感染是宫颈癌和其他肛门生殖器癌症的必要原因,但许多感染会自行清除,因此需要免疫疗法来安全促进持续病例中的病毒清除。该研究旨在确定 HPV16 阳性宫颈上皮内瘤变 ≤1 级女性在 PVX2 免疫治疗后与 HPV16 清除相关的免疫相关性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在临床环境中,对 12 名患有 HPV16 阳性宫颈上皮内瘤变 ≤ 1 级的女性进行了 PVX2 免疫治疗,并随着时间的推移对 免疫应答 进行评估,以评估病毒清除的相关性。
elements_zh.methods: PVX2 由肌内注射 HPV16 E7 靶向 pNGVL4a-Sig/E7(排毒)/HSP70 DNA 疫苗(第 0 周和第 4 周 3 mg)组成,随后是 HPV16 L2E7E6 融合蛋白(TA-CIN;第 8 周 100 μg),疫苗接种 后免疫分析包括抗体滴度、CD8+ T 细胞反应、TCR 多样性和细胞因子测量。
elements_zh.main_results: 第 6 个月时,11 名可评估参与者中有 5 名未检测到 HPV16,而 疫苗接种 后 E6、E7 和 L2 特异性抗体滴度较高,但与清除率不相关。TCR 克隆多样性/扩展和公共克隆型均与 HPV16 清除无关,但在清除 HPV16 的患者中,在 疫苗 后观察到较高比例的 疫苗 抗原特异性读数。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,仅抗体滴度和 TCR 库变化并不能预测 HPV16 清除率,这表明 疫苗 抗原特异性 免疫应答 可能比全局 TCR 指标更相关。他们强调 疫苗 抗原特异性读数的出现是一种潜在的新关联,值得进一步研究。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现谨慎地表明,PVX2 免疫疗法可能会促进一些患有低度病变的女性的 HPV16 清除,从而可能减少对侵入性 监测 的需求以及相关的医疗负担,尽管保护的相关性尚未完全确定。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的样本量较小(n = 12)且缺乏对照组限制了因果推断和普遍性,并且对仅抽象证据的依赖进一步限制了有关清除率免疫相关性的结论的强度。

title: Immunoinformatics-Driven Rational Design of Altered Peptide Ligands and In Vitro Validation of a Multi-Epitope CTL Formulation Targeting HPV16 E6/E7
abstract: Background: Therapeutic vaccination against human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) is frequently limited by the weak HLA-A*02:01 presentation of native E6/E7 oncoprotein epitopes. This study aims to utilize an integrated computational-experimental pipeline to design and evaluate anchor-optimized altered peptide ligands (APLs) for improving peptide presentation and HPV16-specific T-cell responses. Methods: Anchor-residue substitutions were introduced into three wild-type E6/E7 epitopes. Candidates were prioritized in silico based on predicted presentation, affinity, immunogenicity, and toxicity, and subsequently evaluated via in vitro functional assays using HLA-A*02:01-positive donor cells and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Results: Anchor optimization successfully converted weak binders into strong binders; for instance, E6apl improved predicted affinity from 329.33 to 6.21 nM. Crucially, candidate E7apl1 exhibited normal CD8+ T-cell expansion but reduced IFN-γ secretion, revealing a distinct binding–immunogenicity dissociation. MD simulations suggested that altered peptide conformational dynamics may contribute to differences in functional activity. Subsequently, an optimized six-peptide formulation (three APLs and three wild-type epitopes) was assembled. The resulting multi-epitope HPV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (meHPV-CTLs) mediated target-specific cytotoxicity against cervical cancer cells, achieving 74.1% ± 5.1% specific lysis at an effector-to-target ratio of 30:1, which was largely abrogated by HLA class I blockade. Conclusions: These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that stable peptide–MHC binding is a necessary but insufficient condition for optimal T-cell activation. The experimentally characterized multi-epitope formulation provides a proof-of-concept strategy for further preclinical evaluation of HPV16-targeted peptide-based immunotherapies. Moreover, because these anchor-optimized APLs are defined at the sequence level, these sequence-defined APLs may potentially be explored in alternative vaccine delivery platforms, including mRNA-based approaches, in future studies.

abstract_zh: 背景:针对 人乳头瘤病毒 16 型 (HPV16) 的治疗 疫苗接种 经常受到天然 E6/E7 癌蛋白表位较弱的 HLA-A*02:01 呈现的限制。本研究旨在利用集成的计算实验流程来设计和评估锚定优化的改变肽配体 (APL),以改善肽呈递和 HPV16 特异性 T 细胞反应。方法:将锚残基取代引入三个野生型E6/E7表位。根据预测的呈现、亲和力、免疫原性和毒性,在计算机中对候选者进行优先排序,随后使用 HLA-A*02:01 阳性供体细胞和分子动力学 (MD) 模拟通过体外功能测定进行评估。结果:Anchor优化成功将弱Binder转化为强Binder;例如,E6apl 将预测亲和力从 329.33 nM 提高到 6.21 nM。至关重要的是,候选 E7apl1 表现出正常的 CD8+ T 细胞扩增,但减少了 IFN-γ 分泌,揭示了独特的结合-免疫原性解离。MD 模拟表明,改变的肽构象动力学可能导致功能活性的差异。随后,组装了优化的六肽制剂(三个 APL 和三个野生型表位)。由此产生的多表位 HPV 特异性细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (meHPV-CTL) 介导针对 宫颈癌 细胞的靶标特异性细胞毒性,在效应器与靶标比率为 30:1 时实现 74.1% ± 5.1% 的特异性裂解,这在很大程度上被 HLA I 类阻断所消除。结论:这些概念验证结果表明,稳定的肽-MHC 结合是最佳 T 细胞激活的必要但不充分的条件。经过实验表征的多表位制剂为 HPV16 靶向肽免疫疗法的进一步临床前评估提供了概念验证策略。此外,由于这些锚定优化的 APL 是在序列水平上定义的,因此在未来的研究中,这些序列定义的 APL 可能会在替代的 疫苗 递送平台(包括基于 mRNA 的方法)中进行探索。

title: Preclinical Development of ARV-2001, an Intradermally Administered mRNA–Lipid Nanoparticle Immunotherapeutic for the Treatment of HPV-16-Positive Cervical High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions
abstract: Background/Objective: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) is the principal cause of cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (cHSIL) and cervical cancer, yet the established treatments remain limited to ablative or excisional procedures that carry reproductive risk and do not eliminate the underlying infection. We report the preclinical development of ARV-2001, a messenger RNA (mRNA)–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) immunotherapeutic encoding mutated, non-oncogenic HPV-16 E6 and E7 fused to a SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 subdomain enriched in human CD4 helper epitopes, formulated in a novel cholesterol-derived ionizable lipid (ARV-T1). Methods: Interactions of ARV-2001-expressed antigens with p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) were evaluated in human cervical carcinoma cell line C33A, in lentiviral constructs in primary human keratinocytes, and in soft-agar colony-formation assays. ARV-2001 was administrated by intramuscular (IM) or intradermal (ID) injection in naive mice or in the TC-1 tumor models. Tumor size and survival were monitored over time and tumor-infiltrated lymphocytes were characterized by flow cytometry. Intracellular cytokine staining and Elispot were used to evaluate immunogenicity. Results: In vitro, the mutated E6/E7–S2 antigen lost the ability to degrade p53, to deregulate the retinoblastoma (Rb) pathway, and to support anchorage-independent growth, suggesting abrogation of oncogenic activity. The S2 domain and imiquimod administration each augmented antitumor activity and intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the syngeneic HPV-16 E6/E7 TC-1 tumor models. In addition, ID administration of ARV-2001 into TC-1 tumor-bearing mice was superior to IM administration in terms of both tumor growth inhibition and survival. ID vaccination with ARV-2001 in mice consistently elicited a more potent E6/E7-specific T-cell response than the same dose given IM. Dose-escalation studies showed a dose-dependent T cell response against E6/E7 in ID-injected mice. Conclusions: This study supports future human evaluation of intradermally administrated ARV-2001 for treatment of HPV-16+ cHSIL in clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study focuses on the preclinical development of ARV-2001, an mRNA–lipid nanoparticle immunotherapeutic targeting HPV-16. The research highlights the oncogenic activity of HPV-16 E6 and E7 proteins and evaluates the potential of ARV-2001 to abrogate this activity. The study demonstrates that intradermal administration of ARV-2001 in TC-1 tumor models leads to superior tumor growth inhibition and survival compared to intramuscular administration. Additionally, the S2 domain of the antigen and imiquimod administration enhance antitumor immune responses by increasing CD8+ T-cell infiltration and reducing myeloid-derived suppressor cells. These results suggest that ARV-2001 could offer a more effective treatment for HPV-16+ cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (cHSIL) than current ablative or excisional procedures. However, the study is limited to preclinical models, and further human trials are needed to validate these findings.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及 ARV-2001(一种 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒免疫治疗药物)在幼稚小鼠和 TC-1 肿瘤模型(表达 HPV-16 E6/E7 的肿瘤模型)中的临床前开发。

title_zh: ARV-2001 的临床前开发,一种皮内注射 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒免疫疗法,用于治疗 HPV-16 阳性宫颈高级鳞状上皮内病变的 治疗
source_body_en: Background/Objective: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV-16) is the principal cause of cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (cHSIL) and cervical cancer, yet the established treatments remain limited to ablative or excisional procedures that carry reproductive risk and do not eliminate the underlying infection. We report the preclinical development of ARV-2001, a messenger RNA (mRNA)–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) immunotherapeutic encoding mutated, non-oncogenic HPV-16 E6 and E7 fused to a SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 subdomain enriched in human CD4 helper epitopes, formulated in a novel cholesterol-derived ionizable lipid (ARV-T1). Methods: Interactions of ARV-2001-expressed antigens with p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) were evaluated in human cervical carcinoma cell line C33A, in lentiviral constructs in primary human keratinocytes, and in soft-agar colony-formation assays. ARV-2001 was administrated by intramuscular (IM) or intradermal (ID) injection in naive mice or in the TC-1 tumor models. Tumor size and survival were monitored over time and tumor-infiltrated lymphocytes were characterized by flow cytometry. Intracellular cytokine staining and Elispot were used to evaluate immunogenicity. Results: In vitro, the mutated E6/E7–S2 antigen lost the ability to degrade p53, to deregulate the retinoblastoma (Rb) pathway, and to support anchorage-independent growth, suggesting abrogation of oncogenic activity. The S2 domain and imiquimod administration each augmented antitumor activity and intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration while reducing myeloid-derived suppressor cells in the syngeneic HPV-16 E6/E7 TC-1 tumor models. In addition, ID administration of ARV-2001 into TC-1 tumor-bearing mice was superior to IM administration in terms of both tumor growth inhibition and survival. ID vaccination with ARV-2001 in mice consistently elicited a more potent E6/E7-specific T-cell response than the same dose given IM. Dose-escalation studies showed a dose-dependent T cell response against E6/E7 in ID-injected mice. Conclusions: This study supports future human evaluation of intradermally administrated ARV-2001 for treatment of HPV-16+ cHSIL in clinical trials.

title: Epidemiology of Human Papillomavirus in the Middle East and North Africa: A Review of Genotypic Prevalence, Vaccination Challenges, and Non-Cervical Clinical Outcomes
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer. Despite the high global disease burden, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region faces substantial challenges in HPV prevention and control. This narrative review aimed to synthesize existing evidence on the prevalence, genotypic distribution, awareness, vaccination status, clinical outcomes, and the role of HPV in non-cervical malignancies in the MENA region. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched, and 122 studies were included. Findings were synthesized qualitatively and descriptively. Cohort studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were prioritized to support inferences about associations and potential causal relationships. Results: HPV prevalence in the general female population of the MENA region ranged from 4.7% to 53.3%, exceeding 90% in high-risk groups and patients with malignancies. The most common genotypes were HPV16 and HPV18; however, distribution patterns varied across populations. Key risk factors included younger age, multiple sexual partners, early age at first sexual intercourse, smoking, and alcohol consumption. General awareness was low to moderate, and vaccination coverage was very low in most countries. Barriers included lack of knowledge, fear of side effects, religious concerns, and social stigma. Evidence also indicates an association between HPV and non-cervical malignancies (head and neck, esophageal, gastric, breast, and thyroid cancers), with HPV DNA detected in tumor tissues. Conclusions: HPV poses a significant public health challenge in the MENA region, characterized by high prevalence, genotypic diversity, limited knowledge and awareness, and unsatisfactory vaccination coverage. Expanding screening and vaccination through financial support, culturally and religiously appropriate education, and longitudinal studies to monitor genotypic changes and associations with other malignancies are essential measures to reduce the burden of HPV-related diseases in the region.

title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 在中东和北非的 流行病学:基因型 患病率、疫苗接种 挑战和非宫颈临床结果的回顾
source_body_en: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the primary etiological agent of cervical cancer. Despite the high global disease burden, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region faces substantial challenges in HPV prevention and control. This narrative review aimed to synthesize existing evidence on the prevalence, genotypic distribution, awareness, vaccination status, clinical outcomes, and the role of HPV in non-cervical malignancies in the MENA region. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched, and 122 studies were included. Findings were synthesized qualitatively and descriptively. Cohort studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were prioritized to support inferences about associations and potential causal relationships. Results: HPV prevalence in the general female population of the MENA region ranged from 4.7% to 53.3%, exceeding 90% in high-risk groups and patients with malignancies. The most common genotypes were HPV16 and HPV18; however, distribution patterns varied across populations. Key risk factors included younger age, multiple sexual partners, early age at first sexual intercourse, smoking, and alcohol consumption. General awareness was low to moderate, and vaccination coverage was very low in most countries. Barriers included lack of knowledge, fear of side effects, religious concerns, and social stigma. Evidence also indicates an association between HPV and non-cervical malignancies (head and neck, esophageal, gastric, breast, and thyroid cancers), with HPV DNA detected in tumor tissues. Conclusions: HPV poses a significant public health challenge in the MENA region, characterized by high prevalence, genotypic diversity, limited knowledge and awareness, and unsatisfactory vaccination coverage. Expanding screening and vaccination through financial support, culturally and religiously appropriate education, and longitudinal studies to monitor genotypic changes and associations with other malignancies are essential measures to reduce the burden of HPV-related diseases in the region.

title: Willingness to receive cross-border human papillomavirus vaccination among Chinese male university students: a cross-sectional study with statistical indirect-association analysis
abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an important strategy for preventing HPV-related disease among males. Access to male HPV vaccination may involve cross-border health seeking for some university students in mainland China. This study estimated willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination among Chinese male university students and examined associations of HPV-related disease recognition, awareness of cross-border vaccination availability, and demographic and informational characteristics with willingness. Methods A cross-sectional anonymous online survey was conducted between September 2025 and March 2026 among 4,260 male university students in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, and overseas. The primary outcome was willingness to travel at personal expense to Hong Kong or Macao for HPV vaccination. HPV-related disease recognition was assessed using four conditions with established HPV associations: anogenital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Of 4,260 participants, 3,182 (74.69%) reported willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination. Participants with a disease-recognition gap had substantially lower adjusted odds of willingness than those identifying at least one condition (aOR = 0.041, 95% CI: 0.017–0.095; p < 0.001). Awareness of cross-border HPV vaccination availability was positively associated with willingness (aOR = 1.233, 95% CI: 1.056–1.441; p = 0.008). Students studying in Guangdong province had higher adjusted odds of willingness than students in other mainland provinces (aOR = 1.213, 95% CI: 1.045–1.409; p = 0.011). Higher academic grade (aOR per level = 1.111, 95% CI: 1.023–1.206; p = 0.012) and exposure to school-based HPV information (aOR = 1.203, 95% CI: 1.005–1.440; p = 0.044) were also independently associated with willingness. The estimated indirect association through cross-border service awareness was statistically significant but small ( B = −0.022, bootstrap 95% CI: −0.040 to −0.006). Conclusion Willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination was reported by approximately three-quarters of participants. Recognition of established HPV-related male diseases and awareness of cross-border vaccination availability were associated with willingness. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether male-focused HPV education and service-navigation strategies increase actual vaccine uptake.

title_zh: 中国男大学生跨境接受人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种的意愿:统计间接关联分析的横断面研究
source_body_en: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an important strategy for preventing HPV-related disease among males. Access to male HPV vaccination may involve cross-border health seeking for some university students in mainland China. This study estimated willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination among Chinese male university students and examined associations of HPV-related disease recognition, awareness of cross-border vaccination availability, and demographic and informational characteristics with willingness. Methods A cross-sectional anonymous online survey was conducted between September 2025 and March 2026 among 4,260 male university students in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, and overseas. The primary outcome was willingness to travel at personal expense to Hong Kong or Macao for HPV vaccination. HPV-related disease recognition was assessed using four conditions with established HPV associations: anogenital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Of 4,260 participants, 3,182 (74.69%) reported willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination. Participants with a disease-recognition gap had substantially lower adjusted odds of willingness than those identifying at least one condition (aOR = 0.041, 95% CI: 0.017–0.095; p < 0.001). Awareness of cross-border HPV vaccination availability was positively associated with willingness (aOR = 1.233, 95% CI: 1.056–1.441; p = 0.008). Students studying in Guangdong province had higher adjusted odds of willingness than students in other mainland provinces (aOR = 1.213, 95% CI: 1.045–1.409; p = 0.011). Higher academic grade (aOR per level = 1.111, 95% CI: 1.023–1.206; p = 0.012) and exposure to school-based HPV information (aOR = 1.203, 95% CI: 1.005–1.440; p = 0.044) were also independently associated with willingness. The estimated indirect association through cross-border service awareness was statistically significant but small ( B = −0.022, bootstrap 95% CI: −0.040 to −0.006). Conclusion Willingness to receive cross-border HPV vaccination was reported by approximately three-quarters of participants. Recognition of established HPV-related male diseases and awareness of cross-border vaccination availability were associated with willingness. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether male-focused HPV education and service-navigation strategies increase actual vaccine uptake.

title: Analysis of the clinical utility of p16/Ki-67 dual staining in screening cervical lesions among women positive for high-risk HPV
abstract: Cervical cancer is closely associated with persistent infection by high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV). Although HPV testing offers high sensitivity, its limited specificity may result in excessive colposcopy referrals, and the triage performance of traditional liquid-based cytology (TCT) remains suboptimal among hrHPV-positive women. As a biomarker reflecting HPV-mediated cell-cycle dysregulation and aberrant proliferation, p16/Ki-67 dual staining has shown potential advantages in identifying clinically significant high-grade cervical lesions. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical utility of p16/Ki-67 dual staining in screening cervical lesions among hrHPV-positive women and to explore its role in optimizing referral strategies. Retrospectively, this single-center cohort study included 100 consecutive hrHPV-positive women who attended our clinic between October 2024 and October 2025. All participants underwent hrHPV genotyping, TCT, and p16/Ki-67 dual staining during the same visit, followed by colposcopy and histopathological assessment. Histology served as the reference standard. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of p16/Ki-67 for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2+ (CIN2+) lesions and compared it with TCT, HPV genotyping, and a combined triage model (hrHPV + TCT + p16/Ki-67). In addition, we simulated the screening efficiency of different colposcopy referral strategies. Among the 100 hrHPV-positive women included, 35 (35.0%) were diagnosed with CIN2+. title: Fractional-Order Mathematical Modeling of Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) Using Artificial Deep Neural Networks
abstract: The study proposes a mathematical framework to evaluate the HPV infection transmission dynamics, taking into account advanced approaches related to fractional calculus. The HPV infection and cervical cancer is always a major public health threat across the world, particularly in those areas having insufficient availability to health care services and control interventions. In first step, the positivity and boundedness of solutions are precisely examined to show that the model remains biologically valuable in the long run. In this study the disease free equilibrium and endemic equilibrium is provided to describe the long term behavior of the disease in a population. The basic reproductive number and sensitivity analysis is also studied as it is vital to analyse behavior of the dynamics. The theoretical results is establish for the model under consideration using fixed point theory. Next, the condition for Hyers-Ulam’s (H-U) type stability is clearly demonstrated. Then, applying the modified Euler’s method (MEM) for the computation of numerical solution of the proposed model. At the end, we give graphical representation of the involved results. We use some real values for the parameters involved in our considered model. Matlab is used for graphical demonstration. Through a comprehensive numerical analysis, the model explores how various fractional order values inuence the dynamics of HPV transmission. Hence, revealing suggestions for how fractional order may better convey the intricate relationships within the communities. These development also draw awareness to the method’s significance in advancing disease modeling and deepening our knowledge of HPV transmission. With the help of artificial deep neural networks (DNNs), we investigate the considered model. We deduced some statistical thresholds including mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) together with progressional analysis. Further, graphical illustrations are given for infected classes using different fractional order. Absolute error between the simulated and those predicted by DNNs are compared for various fractional orders.

elements_en.main_results: The study demonstrates Hyers-Ulam’s (H-U) type stability conditions for the model and provides graphical representations of infected classes across different fractional orders, comparing absolute errors between simulated and DNN-predicted values.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as revealing how fractional order values influence HPV transmission dynamics, suggesting that fractional calculus may better capture complex community relationships, and highlight the method’s significance in advancing disease modeling.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that fractional-order mathematical modeling combined with artificial neural networks could improve understanding of HPV transmission patterns, potentially informing surveillance and control strategies in resource-limited settings.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is theoretical and abstract-only, lacking empirical validation in human populations or clinical data, which limits its direct applicability to public health practice and warrants a low confidence assessment.

title_zh: 使用人工深度神经网络对人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 进行分数阶数学建模
source_body_en: The study proposes a mathematical framework to evaluate the HPV infection transmission dynamics, taking into account advanced approaches related to fractional calculus. The HPV infection and cervical cancer is always a major public health threat across the world, particularly in those areas having insufficient availability to health care services and control interventions. In first step, the positivity and boundedness of solutions are precisely examined to show that the model remains biologically valuable in the long run. In this study the disease free equilibrium and endemic equilibrium is provided to describe the long term behavior of the disease in a population. The basic reproductive number and sensitivity analysis is also studied as it is vital to analyse behavior of the dynamics. The theoretical results is establish for the model under consideration using fixed point theory. Next, the condition for Hyers-Ulam’s (H-U) type stability is clearly demonstrated. Then, applying the modified Euler’s method (MEM) for the computation of numerical solution of the proposed model. At the end, we give graphical representation of the involved results. We use some real values for the parameters involved in our considered model. Matlab is used for graphical demonstration. Through a comprehensive numerical analysis, the model explores how various fractional order values inuence the dynamics of HPV transmission. Hence, revealing suggestions for how fractional order may better convey the intricate relationships within the communities. These development also draw awareness to the method’s significance in advancing disease modeling and deepening our knowledge of HPV transmission. With the help of artificial deep neural networks (DNNs), we investigate the considered model. We deduced some statistical thresholds including mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) together with progressional analysis. Further, graphical illustrations are given for infected classes using different fractional order. Absolute error between the simulated and those predicted by DNNs are compared for various fractional orders.
abstract_zh: 该研究提出了一个数学框架来评估 HPV 感染 传播 动态,同时考虑到与分数阶微积分相关的先进方法。HPV 感染和 宫颈癌 始终是世界各地的主要公共卫生威胁,特别是在那些医疗保健服务和控制干预措施不足的地区。第一步,精确检查解的正性和有界性,以表明该模型从长远来看仍然具有生物学价值。在本研究中,提供无病平衡和地方病平衡来描述疾病在人群中的长期行为。还研究了基本繁殖数和敏感性分析,因为它对于分析动力学行为至关重要。理论结果是使用不动点理论为所考虑的模型建立的。接下来,清楚地证明了 Hyers-Ulam (H-U) 型稳定性的条件。然后,应用修正欧拉方法(MEM)计算所提出模型的数值解。最后,我们给出了所涉及结果的图形表示。我们对我们考虑的模型中涉及的参数使用一些实际值。使用Matlab进行图形演示。通过全面的数值分析,该模型探讨了各种分数阶值如何影响 HPV 传播 的动态。因此,揭示了分数阶如何更好地传达社区内复杂关系的建议。这些进展也让人们认识到该方法在推进疾病建模和加深我们对 HPV 传播 的了解方面的重要性。在人工深度神经网络 (DNN) 的帮助下,我们研究了所考虑的模型。我们通过渐进分析推导出一些统计阈值,包括均方误差(MSE)和均方根误差(RMSE)。此外,还使用不同的分数阶对受感染类别进行了图示。对不同分数阶的模拟结果和 DNN 预测结果之间的绝对误差进行了比较。

title: The cervicovaginal microbiome: an emerging determinant of HPV infection and disease
abstract: ABSTRACT Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are epitheliotropic viruses that cause diseases ranging from cutaneous warts to invasive cancers. HPVs exhibit tropism for the epithelial lining of the skin, oral cavity, and anogenital tract. A subset of HPVs, known as high-risk HPVs, have oncogenic potential and cause nearly one-third of all virus-associated cancers worldwide, including essentially all cervical cancers, most other anogenital cancers, and a growing percentage of head and neck cancers. A large and growing body of clinical and epidemiological research has established the host microbiome, or the collection of microorganisms on and within the body, as a key determinant of HPV infection, persistence, and disease development. In this review, an overview of the current understanding of associations between bacterial components of the host cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) and aspects of HPV pathogenesis is discussed. Potential mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV infection and neoplastic disease development are also presented. The inherent challenges of studying HPVs and the microbiome have impeded progress to define not only the underlying mechanisms involved in HPV-CVM interactions, but also the ability to address remaining questions such as causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. Emerging in vitro and in vivo models provide powerful opportunities to address these outstanding questions and increase our understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and subsequent disease.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了 宿主 微生物组(特别是 CVM 的细菌成分)的临床和流行病学研究,并讨论了 CVM 影响 HPV 发病机制 的潜在机制。它强调了研究 HPV-微生物组相互作用的挑战以及对先进模型来解决因果关系、时间动态和方向性的需求。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究 HPV 和微生物组的固有挑战阻碍了在定义 HPV-CVM 相互作用的潜在机制以及解决这种关系的因果关系、时间动态和方向性方面取得进展。该评论指出,尽管出现了体外和体内模型,但这些差距仍然存在。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 新兴的体外和体内模型被认为是解决有关 HPV-CVM 相互作用的突出问题(包括因果关系和时间动态)的关键工具,从而增进对导致 HPV 感染和疾病的跨界相互作用的理解。

Potential mechanisms through which the CVM influences HPV infection and neoplastic disease development are also presented. The inherent challenges of studying HPVs and the microbiome have impeded progress to define not only the underlying mechanisms involved in HPV-CVM interactions, but also the ability to address remaining questions such as causality, temporal dynamics, and the directionality of this relationship. Emerging in vitro and in vivo models provide powerful opportunities to address these outstanding questions and increase our understanding of trans-kingdom interactions that contribute to HPV infection and subsequent disease.

title: The Prevalence of Human Papilloma Virus in Turkish Women
abstract: Background/Objectives: The prevalence of Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) in Türkiye may vary from that reported in other countries. Determining the age-specific distribution of HPV infection and its overall prevalence in all tested individuals, supported by a large sample size, would provide valuable insights for HPV prevention programs. This study aims to determine the regional prevalence of HPV infection. Methods: This is a retrospective study containing data from 52,930 patients who underwent HPV testing at a tertiary hospital between 2016 and 2024. Patients aged 21 to 65 were included in the study. Target DNA amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and nucleic acid hybridization techniques were performed for the identification of HPV. Overall prevalence, age-specific prevalence, and genotype distribution were examined. Results: Analysis of genotype distribution revealed that isolated HPV16 positivity was 4.0% (n = 2118), isolated HPV18 positivity was 1.0% (n = 528), and isolated other high-risk (HR) HPV types (excluding HPV16 and HPV18) were detected in 10.8% (n = 5693) of patients. The co-positivity rates were as follows: HPV16 and HPV18 in 0.4% (n = 237), HPV16 and HR-HPV other in 2.3% (n = 1197), HPV18 and HR-HPV other in 1.0% (n = 513), and HPV16, HPV18, and HR-HPV other in 0.3% (n = 145). Conclusions: This study highlights that HPV positivity is higher among individuals aged 21–24 years in our population, the overall prevalence is broadly consistent with the range reported in previous Turkish and international studies, and the pooled other HR-HPV group was more frequent than HPV16 or HPV18 individually.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to characterize the prevalence of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) in Türkiye, noting that reported prevalence may differ from other countries and that age-specific distribution data are valuable for prevention programs.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed HPV test results from 52,930 patients aged 21–65 at a Turkish tertiary hospital (2016–2024) to determine regional prevalence and genotype distribution. Using PCR and nucleic acid hybridization, it found isolated HPV16 in 4.0%, HPV18 in 1.0%, and other high-risk HPV types in 10.8% of patients, with co-infections in up to 2.3%. HPV positivity was highest in the 21–24 age group, and the pooled other HR-HPV group exceeded HPV16 or HPV18 individually. The authors conclude that these patterns are consistent with prior Turkish and international reports. The findings support targeted HPV prevention programs but are limited by retrospective design, single-centre data, and lack of clinical outcomes, warranting cautious interpretation.

title: The human papillomavirus L2 protein in the capsid is an ensemble of related structures poised to exit the virus particle
abstract: The human papillomavirus (HPV) capsid contains 360 molecules of the L1 protein, which assembles into pentamers that form the capsid shell, and up to 72 molecules of the L2 protein. The C-terminus of the L2 protein must emerge from the capsid, insert into the endosome membrane, and protrude into the cytoplasm to bind to cellular proteins that mediate trafficking of the virus to the nucleus during virus entry. Computational analysis predicts that much of L2 is disordered, but the stoichiometry, structure and location of L2 in the capsid remain elusive. Here, we use cryo-EM single particle analysis of HPV16 pseudovirus capsids with and without the L2 protein combined with AlphaFold3 predictions and molecular dynamics simulations to develop a structural model of L2 within the capsid. Our results revealed that a single molecule of L2 associates with the inner surface of most L1 pentamers. The relatively rigid structure of the pentamer forces the long intrinsically disordered segments of L2 to adopt numerous related, compact, stable conformations in the capsid, whereas the structured elements of L2 remain folded but adopt varied positions in space largely beneath the pentamer. A finger-like projection of L2 extends into the central pore of the pentamer, but many different segments of the disordered domains of L2 can form fingers. In some models the C-terminus of L2 extends through the pore to the exterior surface of the capsid positioned to insert into the endosomal membrane. Consistent with these models, analysis of purified pseudoviruses showed that the C-terminus of multiple L2 molecules is exposed on the surface of each capsid. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding how L2 is organized in the capsid poised to initiate its action during virus entry.

abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 衣壳包含 360 个 L1 蛋白分子(可组装成形成衣壳壳的五聚体)和最多 72 个 L2 蛋白分子。L2 蛋白的 C 末端必须从衣壳中出现,插入内体膜,并突出到细胞质中,以与在病毒进入过程中介导病毒运输到细胞核的细胞蛋白结合。计算分析预测 L2 的大部分是无序的,但衣壳中 L2 的化学计量、结构和位置仍然难以捉摸。在这里,我们使用冷冻电镜单粒子分析含有和不含有 L2 蛋白的 HPV16 假病毒衣壳,并结合 AlphaFold3 预测和分子动力学模拟,开发衣壳内 L2 的结构模型。我们的结果表明,L2 的单个分子与大多数 L1 五聚体的内表面结合。五聚体相对刚性的结构迫使L2的长的本质上无序的片段在衣壳中采用许多相关的、紧凑的、稳定的构象,而L2的结构元件保持折叠,但在主要位于五聚体下方的空间中采用不同的位置。L2 的手指状突起延伸到五聚体的中心孔中,但 L2 无序结构域的许多不同片段可以形成手指。在一些模型中,L2 的 C 末端穿过孔延伸至衣壳的外表面,定位为插入内体膜。与这些模型一致,对纯化的假病毒的分析表明,多个 L2 分子的 C 末端暴露在每个衣壳的表面。这些发现为理解 L2 在衣壳中如何组织以在病毒进入期间启动其作用提供了结构基础。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解 HPV 衣壳内 L2 蛋白的结构组织及其在病毒进入中的作用。背景强调了 L2 蛋白在病毒进入细胞核过程中介导转运的重要性。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于了解 HPV 衣壳结构和 L2 蛋白的功能,这可能为未来有关病毒进入机制的研究和靶向治疗或 疫苗 的开发提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算分析和冷冻电镜,在捕获 L2 构象变化的完整动态方面可能存在局限性。然而,证据有多种方法支持,强度中等。

title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus in the public health system of the central-northern region of Chile
abstract: OBJECTIVE Previously, we found a high prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the private health system. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine the frequency of HR-HPV in a large cohort of women attending the public health system and to compare these findings. METHODS A total of 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique. RESULTS The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection between 2020 and 2024 was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with annual values of 13.07%, 12.64%, 14.80%, 14.24%, and 14.15% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. In women under 25 years of age, the prevalence of HR-HPV was 34.03% during the evaluated period, compared to 16.35% in women aged 25 to 44 years, 10.47% in those aged 45 to 64 years, and 11.52% in women over 64 years of age. Pap smears showed 89.71% NILM results in HPV-negative women, compared to 74.59% in HPV-positive women. The rates of LSIL and HSIL were 0.14% and 0.07% in HPV-negative women, respectively; however, these values increased to 4.73% and 4.43% in HPV-positive women, respectively. Probable carcinoma was found in only 0.006% of HPV-negative women, but in 0.46% of HPV-positive women. CONCLUSIONS The prevalence of HR-HPV infection in women attending the public health system in the central-northern region appears to be similar to that previously reported in Chile, but lower than that reported in the same region for women attending the private health system.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to determine the frequency of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in women attending the public health system, as previous research had found a high prevalence in the private health system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study analyzed 39,512 cervical samples from women aged 18 to 91 years who attended gynecological check-ups between 2020 and 2024 in the central-northern region of Chile.
analysis.methods: Samples were analyzed using qPCR and the Papanicolaou technique to detect HR-HPV infection and cytological abnormalities.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of HR-HPV infection was 13.70% (95% CI: 13.37-14.05%), with higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had significantly higher rates of LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) than HPV-negative women.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HR-HPV prevalence in the public health system was similar to previously reported national rates but lower than in the private health system in the same region, highlighting potential disparities in HPV infection rates between healthcare systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings inform public health surveillance and resource allocation by providing age-stratified prevalence data, which can guide targeted screening and prevention strategies for HPV-related diseases in the public health system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength lies in its large sample size and longitudinal design, but limitations include potential selection bias as only women attending gynecological check-ups were included, and the evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the report.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined the prevalence of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) in 39,512 women attending Chile's public health system between 2020-2024. The overall HR-HPV prevalence was 13.70%, with significantly higher rates in women under 25 years (34.03%) compared to older age groups. HPV-positive women had markedly increased rates of cytological abnormalities, including LSIL (4.73% vs. 0.14%) and HSIL (4.43% vs. 0.07%) compared to HPV-negative women. The prevalence was similar to national rates but lower than previously reported in the private health system, suggesting potential healthcare disparities. These findings provide valuable data for public health planning and targeted screening programs.

abstract_zh: 目标 此前,我们发现在私人医疗系统就诊的女性中 高危型HPV (HR-HPV) 的 患病率 较高。因此,本研究的目的是确定在公共卫生系统就诊的大量 队列研究 女性中 HR-HPV 的频率,并比较这些结果。方法 使用 qPCR 和巴氏技术对 2020 年至 2024 年间参加妇科检查的 18 至 91 岁女性的 39,512 份宫颈样本进行分析。结果 2020-2024年HR-HPV感染总体患病率为13.70%(95% CI:13.37-14.05%),2020年、2021年分别为13.07%、12.64%、14.80%、14.24%和14.15%。分别为 2022 年、2023 年和 2024 年。在25岁以下女性中,评估期间HR-HPV的患病率为34.03%,而25至44岁女性为16.35%,45至64岁女性为10.47%,64岁以上女性为11.52%。子宫颈抹片检查显示,HPV 阴性女性的 NILM 结果为 89.71%,而 HPV 阳性女性的 NILM 结果为 74.59%。HPV阴性女性中LSIL和HSIL的发生率分别为0.14%和0.07%;然而,在 HPV 阳性女性中,这些值分别增加到 4.73% 和 4.43%。HPV 阴性女性中只有 0.006% 可能患有癌症,而 HPV 阳性女性中则有 0.46% 可能患有癌症。结论 中北部地区公共卫生系统女性 HR-HPV 感染 患病率 似乎与智利之前报告的相似,但低于同一地区私营医疗系统女性报告的 患病率。

title: HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Imaging Framework for AJCC Version 9 TNM Staging
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is biologically and prognostically distinct from HPV-negative disease, and staging directly impacts treatment. The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control version 9 TNM staging system incorporates unequivocal imaging-detected and/or clinically detected extranodal extension (iENE) into clinical nodal staging and definitive pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging. Additionally, it provides more explicit anatomic definitions for advanced local disease (clinical T4) while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. Radiologists play a central role in the multidisciplinary team by evaluating endophytic tumor extent, regional nodal disease and iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET. This article reviews clinically relevant oropharyngeal anatomy and proposes a practical radiologic approach to assigning T, N, and M categories in HPV-associated OPSCC. It emphasizes cautious interpretation of iENE because of interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance, with further high-grade evidence needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier. It also highlights multidisciplinary factors that guide selection of surgical resection versus nonsurgical therapy. Posttreatment evaluation is discussed in the context of blood-based biomarkers such as tumor tissue-modified viral HPV DNA. The goal of this article is to provide a practical, staging-focused imaging framework for evaluation of HPV-associated OPSCC. Keywords: CT, MR Imaging, Head/Neck, Neck, Pharynx, Surgery, Human Papillomavirus, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Oropharynx, Transoral Robotic Surgery, Oropharyngeal Carcinoma, TTMV HPV DNA © RSNA, 2026.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), focusing on the role of imaging in the AJCC version 9 TNM staging system, specifically evaluating T, N, and M categories and extranodal extension (iENE) in HPV-positive disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The article is a narrative review that outlines a radiologic approach to staging HPV-associated OPSCC, emphasizing the evaluation of tumor extent, nodal disease, iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET, and discusses multidisciplinary factors guiding treatment selection.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review confirms that AJCC version 9 incorporates iENE into clinical nodal staging and pathologic extranodal extension into pathologic nodal staging for HPV-associated OPSCC, while maintaining T and M category definitions from the eighth edition.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance in interpreting iENE, noting that high-grade evidence is needed to establish its consistently reproducible, incremental prognostic value as a clinical N category modifier.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review underscores the need for further high-grade evidence to validate the prognostic utility of iENE and calls for cautious interpretation in clinical practice, while also emphasizing the central role of radiologists in multidisciplinary teams for accurate staging and treatment planning.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an imaging framework for AJCC version 9 TNM staging of HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), emphasizing the distinct biological and prognostic features of HPV-positive disease. It details the incorporation of imaging-detected extranodal extension (iENE) into nodal staging and the maintenance of T and M category definitions from the eighth edition. The review highlights the central role of radiologists in evaluating tumor extent, nodal disease, iENE, and distant metastasis using CT, MRI, and PET, while also discussing multidisciplinary factors guiding treatment selection. A key controversy is the interreader variability and imperfect diagnostic performance of iENE, with a call for high-grade evidence to confirm its prognostic value. The review concludes by emphasizing the need for further validation of iENE and the importance of radiologists in accurate staging and treatment planning.

title: Correlation Between Prognostic Indicators, HPV Status, and Cancer Stem Cell Markers in a Population of Human Tongue Carcinomas.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a significant public health issue. While tobacco and alcohol are established risk factors, the role of human papillomavirus (HPV) in oral carcinogenesis remains debated. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are implicated in tumor aggressiveness and therapy resistance. This study investigated the correlation between HPV infection, CSC marker expression (CD44, CD98, ALDH1), and clinicopathological parameters in tongue SCCs. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 1047 OSCC cases (2013-2018) was reviewed. From 452 tongue SCCs, 83 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded specimens were randomly selected. HPV DNA detection was performed using qPCR with generic and type-specific primers (HPV 6, 11, 16, 18). Immunohistochemical expression of CD44, CD98, and ALDH1 was evaluated and quantified using digital image analysis (IHC Profiler). Statistical analyses included Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square, and Spearman correlation tests. RESULTS: HPV DNA was detected in 2/83 cases (2.4%): one HPV16-positive and one with co-infection (HPV6/18). CD44 expression was ubiquitously high, with no significant difference between -High and -Positive categories (p > 0.9999), but both were significantly higher than -Low and -Negative scores (p < 0.0001). ALDH1 exhibited a focal staining pattern. The ALDH1-High score was significantly less frequent than -Positive and -Low scores (p < 0.01) and showed a significant positive correlation with both advanced clinical stage (Spearman r: 0.5062; p = 0.0007) and higher tumor grade (Spearman r: 0.3352; p = 0.0322). CD98 was not detected. An inverse correlation was observed between HPV and clinical staging (Spearman r: -0.2377; p = 0.0305); however, due to the low number of HPV-positive cases, this finding must be interpreted with caution. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest a distinct CSC expression profile in this cohort, characterized by ubiquitous CD44 expression and a rare but highly aggressive ALDH1-High subpopulation, concomitant with low HPV detection. The strong positive correlation of ALDH1-High score with advanced stage and grade highlights its potential role as a key driver of tumor aggression, warranting further investigation as a prognostic marker.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study aimed to investigate the correlation between human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, cancer stem cell (CSC) marker expression (CD44, CD98, ALDH1), and clinicopathological parameters in tongue squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs). The focus was on HPV types and explicitly HPV-associated diseases, with a particular emphasis on the role of HPV in oral carcinogenesis and its relationship with CSC markers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study was a retrospective cohort analysis of 1047 OSCC cases (2013-2018), with 83 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded specimens randomly selected. HPV DNA detection was conducted using qPCR with generic and type-specific primers (HPV 6, 11, 16, 18). Immunohistochemical expression of CD44, CD98, and ALDH1 was evaluated using digital image analysis (IHC Profiler). Statistical analyses included Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-square, and Spearman correlation tests.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV DNA was detected in only 2/83 cases (2.4%), with one being HPV16-positive and another showing co-infection with HPV6/18. CD44 expression was universally high, with no significant difference between high and positive categories. ALDH1-High scores were significantly less frequent and correlated with advanced clinical stage and higher tumor grade. CD98 was not detected. The study suggests a distinct CSC expression profile in tongue SCCs, with ALDH1-High being a potential marker for tumor aggression.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that the inverse correlation between HPV and clinical staging (Spearman r: -0.2377; p = 0.0305) must be interpreted cautiously due to the low number of HPV-positive cases. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The strong positive correlation between ALDH1-High scores and advanced stage and grade highlights the need for further investigation into ALDH1 as a prognostic marker. abstract_zh: 背景:口腔鳞状细胞癌(OSCC)是一个重要的公共卫生问题。虽然烟草和酒精是既定的危险因素,但 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 在口腔癌发生中的作用仍存在争议。癌症干细胞(CSC)与肿瘤侵袭性和治疗耐药性有关。本研究调查了 HPV 感染、CSC 标志物表达(CD44、CD98、ALDH1)和舌 SCC 临床病理参数之间的相关性。方法:对 2013-2018 年 1047 例 OSCC 病例进行回顾性 队列研究 分析。从452例舌SCC中随机抽取83例福尔马林固定石蜡包埋标本。使用 qPCR 和通用引物和类型特异性引物(HPV 6、11、16、18)进行 HPV DNA 检测。使用数字图像分析(IHC Profiler)评估和定量 CD44、CD98 和 ALDH1 的免疫组织化学表达。统计分析包括 Kaplan-Meier 生存曲线、Kruskal-Wallis、卡方和 Spearman 相关检验。结果:2/83 例 (2.4%) 中检测到 HPV DNA:1 例 HPV16 阳性,1 例合并感染 (HPV6/18)。CD44 表达普遍较高,-High 和 -Positive 类别之间没有显着差异 (p > 0.9999),但两者均显着高于 -Low 和 -Negative 得分 (p < 0.0001)。ALDH1 表现出局灶性染色模式。ALDH1-高分明显低于-阳性和-低分(p < 0.01),并且与晚期临床分期(Spearman r:0.5062;p = 0.0007)和较高的肿瘤分级(Spearman r:0.3352;p = 0.0322)呈显着正相关。未检测到 CD98。HPV 与临床分期之间观察到负相关(Spearman r:-0.2377;p = 0.0305);然而,由于 HPV 阳性病例数量较少,必须谨慎解释这一发现。结论:我们的研究结果表明,队列研究 中存在独特的 CSC 表达谱,其特征是普遍存在的 CD44 表达和罕见但高度侵袭性的 ALDH1-High 亚群,同时伴有低 HPV 检测。ALDH1-High 评分与晚期分期和分级的强正相关性凸显了其作为肿瘤侵袭的关键驱动因素的潜在作用,值得作为预后标志物进行进一步研究。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究是对 2013-2018 年 1047 例 OSCC 病例进行回顾性 队列研究 分析,随机选择 83 例福尔马林固定石蜡包埋标本。使用 qPCR 和通用引物和类型特异性引物(HPV 6、11、16、18)进行 HPV DNA 检测。使用数字图像分析(IHC Profiler)评估 CD44、CD98 和 ALDH1 的免疫组织化学表达。统计分析包括 Kaplan-Meier 生存曲线、Kruskal-Wallis、卡方和 Spearman 相关检验。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 仅 2/83 例(2.4%)检测到 HPV DNA,其中 1 例为 HPV16 阳性,另一例显示同时感染 HPV6/18。CD44表达普遍较高,高表达和阳性类别之间没有显着差异。ALDH1-高分出现的频率明显较低,并且与晚期临床分期和较高的肿瘤分级相关。未检测到 CD98。该研究表明舌 SCC 中存在独特的 CSC 表达谱,其中 ALDH1-High 是肿瘤侵袭的潜在标志物。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究指出,由于 HPV 阳性病例数量较少,必须谨慎解释 HPV 与临床分期之间的负相关性(Spearman r:-0.2377;p = 0.0305)。此外,HPV 在口腔癌发生中的作用仍存在争议,该研究没有提供足够的证据来明确解决这一争议。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: ALDH1-High 分数与晚期阶段和等级之间的强正相关性突出表明需要进一步研究 ALDH1 作为预后标志物。舌鳞状细胞癌中 HPV 的检出率较低,表明 HPV 可能不是这种特定癌症类型的主要驱动因素,但需要更多的研究来证实这一点,并探索所观察到的相关性背后的机制。

title: HPV vaccine awareness, uptake, intention, and influencing factors among medical students in Anhui, China: A cross-sectional study
abstract: ABSTRACT Although prophylactic vaccination is highly effective against human papillomavirus (HPV), HPV vaccine uptake among Chinese college students remains insufficient, and evidence among medical university students, particularly males, remains limited. Following the recent approval of male HPV vaccines in China, this study evaluated vaccine awareness, acceptance, and potential barriers among both sexes. A cross-sectional online survey of 831 full-time undergraduate students at Anhui Medical University was conducted from October to December 2025. While overall HPV vaccine awareness was high (88.33%), the actual vaccination rate remained low at 25.55% (54.40% among females). Overall vaccination intention was 67.27%, exhibiting a profound gender disparity (92.80% in females vs. 46.27% in males, P < .001). Multivariable analyses showed that female vaccination uptake was significantly associated with familial socioeconomic factors, particularly monthly living allowance and maternal educational attainment. In male students, neutral or opposing attitudes toward a national male HPV vaccination policy were associated with lower vaccination intention (OR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.409–0.898; OR = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.084–0.756), whereas a maximum acceptable vaccine cost of RMB 1,000–2,000 was associated with higher intention (OR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.003–2.592). Additionally, female students showed higher HPV-related knowledge scores and greater reliance on interpersonal and professional information sources. Ultimately, these findings suggest that improving HPV vaccine uptake among medical university students in China may require targeted educational strategies and more accessible vaccination support, particularly for male students and those with fewer socioeconomic resources.

title: Nondiffuse p16 Expression in HPV-Associated and HPV-Independent Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinomas
abstract: Negative or focal p16 expression may occur in cervical squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) associated with high-risk or low-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), as well as in HPV-independent SCCs. However, this phenomenon is uncommon, and its pathologic and molecular characteristics remain poorly defined. In this single-institution study, we identified 11 cases (11/201 [5.5%]) with negative or focal p16 expression, including 4 (2.0%) associated with high-risk HPV, 6 (3.0%) HPV-independent, and 1 (0.5%) associated with low-risk HPV. Among the 4 high-risk HPV-associated SCCs with complete loss of p16 expression, 3 showed complete loss of the methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP). Notably, MTAP loss was also observed in 2 of 4 p16-negative high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSILs), suggesting that p16/MTAP codeletion may occur at both precursor and invasive stages. In contrast, all 6 HPV-independent SCCs retained MTAP expression. Two HPV-independent SCCs were associated with precursor lesions: 1 resembled verruciform acanthotic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (vaVIN), while the other was analogous to HSIL. Consistent with high-risk HPV infection, all 4 HPV-associated SCCs demonstrated partial or complete loss of RB1 expression. In comparison, only 2 of 6 HPV-independent SCCs showed partial RB1 loss, likely through HPV-independent mechanisms. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the occurrence and characteristics of nondiffuse p16 expression in cervical squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) and those that are HPV-independent.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-institution study analyzed 201 cervical SCC cases, including 4 high-risk HPV-associated, 1 low-risk HPV-associated, and 6 HPV-independent SCCs, to identify patterns of p16 expression and its association with other molecular features.
analysis.methods: The study used immunohistochemistry to assess p16 expression and evaluated molecular characteristics such as MTAP, RB1, p53, and TERT promoter mutations in the identified cases.
analysis.main_results: Nondiffuse p16 expression was observed in 11 cases (5.5%), with 4 associated with high-risk HPV, 1 with low-risk HPV, and 6 HPV-independent. Among the HPV-associated cases, 3 showed complete loss of MTAP, and all 4 demonstrated partial or complete loss of RB1 expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that p16/MTAP codeletion may occur in both precursor and invasive stages of cervical SCCs, highlighting the need for further investigation into the molecular mechanisms underlying this phenomenon.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results emphasize the importance of considering both p16 immunohistochemistry and HPV status when diagnosing cervical SCCs, as nondiffuse p16 expression may indicate different molecular pathways and clinical outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single institution, and the small number of cases with nondiffuse p16 expression may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the occurrence and characteristics of nondiffuse p16 expression in cervical squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) and those that are HPV-independent.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This single-institution study analyzed 201 cervical SCC cases, including 4 high-risk HPV-associated, 1 low-risk HPV-associated, and 6 HPV-independent SCCs, to identify patterns of p16 expression and its association with other molecular features.
analysis_en.methods: The study used immunohistochemistry to assess p16 expression and evaluated molecular characteristics such as MTAP, RB1, p53, and TERT promoter mutations in the identified cases.
analysis_en.main_results: Nondiffuse p16 expression was observed in 11 cases (5.5%), with 4 associated with high-risk HPV, 1 with low-risk HPV, and 6 HPV-independent. Among the HPV-associated cases, 3 showed complete loss of MTAP, and all 4 demonstrated partial or complete loss of RB1 expression.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that p16/MTAP codeletion may occur in both precursor and invasive stages of cervical SCCs, highlighting the need for further investigation into the molecular mechanisms underlying this phenomenon.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results emphasize the importance of considering both p16 immunohistochemistry and HPV status when diagnosing cervical SCCs, as nondiffuse p16 expression may indicate different molecular pathways and clinical outcomes.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single institution, and the small number of cases with nondiffuse p16 expression may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

title_zh: HPV 相关和 HPV 独立的宫颈鳞状细胞癌中非弥漫性 p16 表达
source_body_en: Negative or focal p16 expression may occur in cervical squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) associated with high-risk or low-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), as well as in HPV-independent SCCs. However, this phenomenon is uncommon, and its pathologic and molecular characteristics remain poorly defined. In this single-institution study, we identified 11 cases (11/201 [5.5%]) with negative or focal p16 expression, including 4 (2.0%) associated with high-risk HPV, 6 (3.0%) HPV-independent, and 1 (0.5%) associated with low-risk HPV. Among the 4 high-risk HPV-associated SCCs with complete loss of p16 expression, 3 showed complete loss of the methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP). Notably, MTAP loss was also observed in 2 of 4 p16-negative high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSILs), suggesting that p16/MTAP codeletion may occur at both precursor and invasive stages. In contrast, all 6 HPV-independent SCCs retained MTAP expression. Two HPV-independent SCCs were associated with precursor lesions: 1 resembled verruciform acanthotic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (vaVIN), while the other was analogous to HSIL. Consistent with high-risk HPV infection, all 4 HPV-associated SCCs demonstrated partial or complete loss of RB1 expression. In comparison, only 2 of 6 HPV-independent SCCs showed partial RB1 loss, likely through HPV-independent mechanisms. A wild-type p53 immunostaining pattern was observed in all cases except 1 HPV-independent SCC (case 7), which exhibited a null pattern and harbored a TP53 nonsense mutation (c.430C>T; p.Gln144Ter). p16 promoter methylation was detected in case 9 (HPV-independent SCC). Somatic TERT promoter mutations were identified in 2 of 4 (50%) HPV-associated SCCs, including c.-131C>T, c.-148C>T, and c.-150C>T. Among HPV-independent SCCs, 4 of 6 cases (66.7%) harbored pathogenic TERT promoter mutations, including c.-138C>T (n=1) and c.-124C>T (n=3). No PIK3CA hotspot mutations were detected in p16-negative, high-risk HPV-associated SCCs. In contrast, 2 HPV-independent SCCs harbored PIK3CA hotspot mutations (p.E545K and p.H1047R), supporting a role for PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling in this setting. Because nondiffuse p16 expression can occur in both HPV-associated (high-risk and low-risk HPV) and HPV-independent cervical SCCs, which may have different clinical outcomes, awareness of this phenomenon is important when interpreting negative p16 immunostaining. Although data are limited, routine assessment of both p16 immunohistochemistry and HPV status, or correlation with prior liquid-based HPV test results when available, is recommended.

title: Oncoviruses at the Crossroads of Ageing and Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms and Key Signalling Pathways.
abstract: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current knowledge on HPV's role in ageing and cancer. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus that oncoviruses, including HPV, actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that the convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, but the evidence does not report specific controversies or conflicting findings. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Understanding these interconnected pathways may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations. elements_zh.scope_and_question: 这篇综述探讨了 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 与衰老和癌症关键标志相交叉的分子机制,重点关注桥接这些过程的信号通路。核心问题是 HPV 如何调节 宿主 细胞通路以促进持续感染、免疫逃避和恶性转化,重点是其在与年龄相关的细胞功能障碍中的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 HPV 在衰老和癌症中作用的当前知识的叙述性综合。它不报告特定的数据库、搜索日期或荟萃分析方法。这些证据源自对 HPV 及其分子相互作用的现有文献的一般科学理解和解释。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人们一致认为,包括 HPV 在内的肿瘤病毒会主动重编程 宿主 信号网络,以促进持续感染、免疫逃避和恶性转化。p53、mTOR、NF-κB、PI3K/AKT 和 Wnt/β-连环蛋白等中央通路经常成为病毒蛋白的目标,导致细胞存活、增殖和衰老失调。这些相互作用导致肿瘤发生和衰老相关的细胞功能障碍。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,病毒肿瘤发生、衰老和癌症的趋同反映了共同的分子机制,但证据并未报告具体的争议或相互矛盾的发现。对于病毒诱导的肿瘤微环境调节的精确机制和宿主 免疫应答缺乏详细的讨论。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 了解这些相互关联的途径可能会揭示预防和治疗老龄化人群中与病毒相关的恶性肿瘤的新治疗靶点和策略。该综述表明,需要进一步研究来探索病毒诱导的肿瘤微环境调节与 宿主 免疫应答 之间的动态相互作用。

title_zh: 处于衰老和癌症十字路口的肿瘤病毒:分子机制和关键信号通路。
source_body_en: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

title: Male genital lichen sclerosus
abstract: Male genital lichen sclerosus (MGLSc) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis that may lead to phimosis, urethral disease, sexual dysfunction and penile squamous cell carcinoma (PeSCC). Although its aetiology remains incompletely understood, clinical and epidemiological observations increasingly support a central role for chronic occluded exposure of susceptible epithelium to urine. The distribution of lesions to occluded, urine-exposed sites, the high rate of remission after circumcision, the rarity of disease in neonatally circumcised populations, the association with microincontinence and urological procedures, and the occurrence of lesions at urinary stoma sites all suggest an irritative pathogenesis. Secondary inflammatory, fibrotic and epithelial repair processes appear to arise downstream of this primary insult. Clinically, MGLSc presents with pallor, erythema, fissuring and progressive scarring, often accompanied by subtle urethral abnormalities contributing to post-micturition dribbling. Long-standing disease may result in meatal stenosis, urethral strictures and functional impairment. A well-recognised association exists between MGLSc, differentiated penile intraepithelial neoplasia and PeSCC, representing a carcinogenic pathway that is typically independent of human papillomavirus infection and ultraviolet radiation. Management aims to control inflammation, restore the epithelial barrier and reduce occlusion. Potent topical corticosteroids remain first-line therapy, while circumcision is highly effective when topical therapy fails. Additional medical and surgical treatments may be required in refractory or complicated disease. This review summarizes current knowledge on the clinical features, pathophysiology, malignant potential and management of MGLSc, with emphasis on mechanisms related to occlusion and urinary exposure.
journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology

analysis.scope_and_question: The scope examines male genital lichen sclerosus (MGLSc), a chronic inflammatory dermatosis of the penis, focusing on its clinical manifestations, potential progression to penile squamous cell carcinoma (PeSCC), and the central question of its pathogenesis and management. The disease is characterized by chronic inflammation, scarring, and functional impairment, with a debated aetiology and carcinogenic potential.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes current knowledge on MGLSc, emphasizing mechanisms related to occlusion and urinary exposure. It integrates clinical observations, epidemiological patterns, and management strategies without reporting systematic search methods, eligibility criteria, or study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Chronic occluded exposure of susceptible epithelium to urine is increasingly supported as a primary aetiological factor in MGLSc. Secondary inflammatory, fibrotic, and epithelial repair processes arise downstream of this insult. Clinically, MGLSc presents with pallor, erythema, fissuring, and scarring, often with subtle urethral abnormalities. Long-standing disease may lead to meatal stenosis, urethral strictures, and functional impairment.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The aetiology of MGLSc remains incompletely understood, with unresolved questions about the relative contributions of chronic urinary exposure versus other potential triggers. The review highlights gaps in understanding the precise mechanisms linking chronic inflammation to malignant transformation, particularly the carcinogenic pathway independent of human papillomavirus infection and ultraviolet radiation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Research priorities include elucidating the molecular and cellular pathways linking chronic urinary exposure to inflammation and fibrosis, and clarifying the mechanisms underlying the progression from MGLSc to PeSCC. Clinically, emphasis should be placed on early diagnosis and intervention to prevent complications such as meatal stenosis and urethral strictures.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines male genital lichen sclerosus (MGLSc), a chronic inflammatory penile dermatosis with potential progression to penile squamous cell carcinoma (PeSCC). The aetiology is increasingly linked to chronic occluded exposure of susceptible epithelium to urine, supported by clinical and epidemiological observations. Secondary inflammatory and fibrotic processes arise downstream of this primary insult. Clinically, MGLSc presents with pallor, erythema, fissuring, and scarring, often with urethral abnormalities. Long-standing disease may result in meatal stenosis, urethral strictures, and functional impairment. The review highlights unresolved questions about the precise mechanisms of disease initiation and progression to malignancy, independent of human papillomavirus infection. Research priorities include elucidating molecular pathways linking urinary exposure to inflammation and fibrosis, and clarifying the carcinogenic mechanisms underlying PeSCC development.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了 MGLSc 的当前知识,强调了与闭塞和尿液暴露相关的机制。它整合了临床观察、流行病学模式和管理策略,无需报告系统搜索方法、资格标准或研究计数。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 越来越多的证据表明,易感上皮细胞长期闭塞地暴露于尿液是 MGLSc 的主要病因。继发性炎症、纤维化和上皮修复过程出现在这种损伤的下游。临床上,MGLSc 表现为苍白、红斑、裂痕和疤痕,通常伴有轻微的尿道异常。长期患病可能导致尿道口狭窄、尿道狭窄和功能障碍。

title: Purification of Disassembled Capsid Protein by Hydroxyapatite Chromatography Enhances Virus-Like Particle Recovery.
abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) are a promising modality with extensive applications in prophylactic and therapeutic vaccine design. Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines are one such example where VLP vaccine applications have led to the successful reduction in HPV-associated diseases, such as cervical cancer. Current purification approaches utilize hydroxyapatite (HA) chromatography in bind-and-elute mode to purify HPV VLPs from host-cell impurities such as proteins and nucleic acids, though binding capacity for VLPs is low due to mass transfer limitations related to their large particle size. The intent of this work was to utilize VLP disassembly prior to HA chromatography in order to increase column yield and capacity. Since L1 protein subunits demonstrated weaker binding avidity for HA resin compared to VLPs, this enabled flow-through purification of L1 protein from strongly adsorbed host cell impurities. Mobile phase conditions were evaluated in batch partition screening experiments to determine the optimal conditions for L1 protein recovery with selective clearance of nucleic acid. Dynamic loading studies showed that while nucleic acid removal was equivalent to the VLP purification process, the flow-through process with disassembled L1 protein achieved higher L1 yield and column capacity. Optimal conditions were applied to HA flow-through purification for multiple HPV types with recombinant L1 protein expressed in yeast, demonstrating > 35% increased yield for six of eight types. The purified, disassembled proteins were subsequently reassembled and had comparable product attributes to the VLP purification process. The implementation of disassembly prior to purification also eliminates the requirement to perform a distinct final disassembly/reassembly process after isolating crude VLPs during purification.
